articles.title: Fritz OS 8.50 macht deine Fritzbox zum Smart-TV-Werbeblocker
articles.text:
Werbung im Smart-TV-Menü? So kann die Fritzbox das jetzt einfach blockieren
Egal welcher Hersteller oder welches Betriebssystem: Mittlerweile spielen eigentlich alle Smart-TVs ab Werk Werbung direkt auf dem Homescreen ab. Für die Hersteller der Geräte ist das ein Milliardengeschäft. Nicht zuletzt, weil die Konsument:innen diese Anzeigen nicht einfach durch Werbeblocker unterbinden können, wie es etwa auf einem Desktop-Rechner möglich wäre.
Dabei gibt es durchaus technische Lösungen, um den Abruf von Werbeanzeigen im gesamten Heimnetzwerk zu unterbinden – und damit eben auch auf dem Smart-TV. Eine beliebte Lösung dafür ist die Software Pi-Hole. Die bietet euch eine Vielzahl an Optionen, um gezielt Verbindungen zu Werbe-Domains zu unterbinden. Allerdings hat das Ganze auch seine Nachteile.
Ihr benötigt einen Raspberry Pi oder einen anderen Computer, der permanent aktiviert sein muss, damit Pi-Hole funktioniert. Außerdem solltet ihr zumindest über rudimentäre Linux- oder Docker-Kenntnisse verfügen, um die Software installieren zu können.
Besitzer einer Fritzbox können auf ein so kompliziertes Setup zukünftig allerdings verzichten. Denn ab Fritz OS 8.40 beziehungsweise 8.50 könnt ihr direkt auf den Routern des deutschen Herstellers Filterlisten hinterlegen, mit denen auch der Abruf von Werbeanzeigen durch euren Smart-TV unterbunden werden kann.
DNS-Filter erklärt: So funktioniert das Ganze technisch
Wann immer wir eine Web-Adresse wie etwa google.com aufrufen, kommt der sogenannte Domain Name Service (DNS) zum Einsatz. Den können wir uns als eine Art Telefonbuch für das Internet vorstellen. Denn eigentlich haben Geräte im Internet keinen Namen, sondern eine Nummer. Das ist die IP-Adresse.
Über einen DNS-Server erfährt unser Computer automatisch, welche IP-Adresse er für Google anwählen muss. Das erspart uns Menschen, dass wir uns komplizierte Ziffernfolgen merken müssen.
Genau diesen Mechanismus nutzt die neue DNS-Filterfunktion der Fitzbox aus. Denn bevor eine Anfrage an den externen DNS-Server geleitet wird, überprüft die Router-Software anhand einer vorab festgelegten Liste, welche Domain-Namen gar nicht erst weitergeleitet werden sollen.
Wenn also euer Smart-TV unter einer Domain des Geräteherstellers nachfragt, welche Anzeige er im Menü ausspielen soll, bleibt die Antwort aus. Da keine Werbung ankommt, kann der Fernseher also auch keine Anzeigen.
Welche Fritzboxen unterstützen das neue Feature?
Standardmäßig sind DNS-Filter ab Fritz OS 8.50 verfügbar. Die Version ist vorläufig aber nur für die Fritzbox 7690 verfügbar. Habt ihr dieses Modell, müsst ihr lediglich darauf achten, dass die neuste Software-Version auf eurem Router installiert ist. Das könnt ihr herausfinden, indem ihr in der Seitenleiste auf System klickt und dann auf Update.
Bei anderen Fritzbox-Modellen müsst ihr allerdings nicht zwingend auf das Update auf 8.50 warten. Stattdessen könnt ihr nämlich die Betaversion Fritz OS 8.40 installieren. Da die Software noch nicht ganz den Ansprüchen des Herstellers genügt, wird sie allerdings nicht automatisch auf eurer Fritzbox installiert.
Ihr könnt Fritz OS 8.40 aber von der Hersteller-Website herunterladen und manuell installieren. Wir hatten mit der Software keine nennenswerten Probleme. Wer aber auf Nummer sicher gehen möchte, der sollte auf die Veröffentlichung von Version 8.50 für den eigenen Router-Typ warten.
Diese Glasfaser-Fritzboxen unterstützen Fritz OS 8.40:
- 5690 Pro
- 5690 XGS
- 5690
- 5590 Fiber
Diese DSL-Fritzboxen unterstützen Fritz OS 8.40:
- 7690
- 7630
- 7590 AX
- 7590
- 7530 AX
Diese Kabel-Fritzboxen unterstützen Fritz OS 8.40:
- 6690 Cable
- 6670 Cable
- 6660 Cable
Diese Kabel-Fritzboxen unterstützen Fritz OS 8.40:
- 4690
- 4050
Diese Mobilfunk-Fritzboxen unterstützen Fritz OS 8.40:
- 6850 5G
- 6850 5G v2
- 6850 4G
- 6850 LTE
So installiert ihr die Laborversion von Fritz OS 8.40 auf eurer Fritzbox
Wie bereits erwähnt müsst ihr die Vorabversion von Fritz OS 8.40 von der Labor-Website von Fritz herunterladen. Dazu wählt ihr auf der Website zunächst euer Fritzbox-Modell aus. Wenn ihr euch nicht sicher seid, welches Modell ihr habt, könnt ihr auf der Unterseite des Geräts nachschauen. Alternativ findet ihr die genaue Produktbezeichnung auch in der oberen Menüleiste des Web-Interface eures Fritzbox-Routers.
Habt ihr die passende Version heruntergeladen, müsst ihr das ZIP-Archiv entpacken. Anschließend wechselt ihr in das Web-Interface eurer Fritzbox. Die erreicht ihr standardmäßig über die Adresse http://192.168.178.1/
Nach der Anmeldung wählt ihr im linken Seitenmenü erst System und dann Update aus. Anschließend klickt ihr auf den rechten Reiter mit dem Titel FRITZ!OS-Datei. Jetzt klickt ihr auf den Button Update aus Datei starten und wählt den Ordner aus, in den ihr die heruntergeladene ZIP-Datei entpackt habt. Anschließend wählt ihr die Datei mit der Endung .image aus.
Im nächsten Schritt wird eure Fritzbox fragen, ob ihr ein Backup eurer aktuellen Einstellungen abspeichern wollt. Das solltet ihr unbedingt bejahen – für den Fall, dass doch etwas schiefgeht.
Der gesamte Installationsprozess dürfte ein paar Minuten dauern, da sich der Router nach dem Update einmal neustartet. Das Browserfenster könnt ihr aber ruhig offenlassen. Nach dem erfolgreichen Update solltet ihr hier direkt weitermachen können.
So findet ihr Filterlisten für euren Smart-TV und richtet sie auf eurer Fritzbox ein
Jetzt seid ihr bereit, eigene DNS-Filterlisten auf eurer Fritzbox zu installieren. Entsprechende Listen finden sich einige im Netz. Eine gute erste Anlaufstelle ist in jedem Fall die von einem deutschen IT-Berater gepflegte Liste hagezi/dns-blocklists auf Github.
Hier findet ihr unter anderem auch DNS-Filterlisten für verschiedene Smart-TV-Betriebssysteme wie RokuOS, Amazons FireOS oder webOS von LG. In unserem Test funktionierte die Roku-Liste ohne Probleme, um den großen Werbebanner auf dem Roku-Homescreen zu blockieren. Mit einem Smart-TV von Samsung hatten wir hingegen mit dieser Filterliste besseren Erfolg.
Wichtig ist in jedem Fall, dass ihr den Link zu der gewünschten Filterliste kopiert und dann zurück ins Web-Interface eurer Fritzbox wechselt. Dort klickt ihr auf Heimnetzwerk und dann auf Netzwerk. Jetzt wählt ihr den Reiter Netzwerkeinstellungen, scrollt ganz nach unten und klickt auf Erweiterte Netzwerkeinstellungen ändern.
Danach wählt ihr den Reiter DNS-Filter und klickt auf Filterliste hinzufügen. Jetzt vergebt ihr einen passenden Namen für die Liste, fügt die kopierte URL in dem Feld darunter ein und klickt auf Hinzufügen. Aber Achtung: Noch ist die Filterliste nicht aktiv. Dazu müsst ihr noch einmal ganz nach unten scrollen und auf Übernehmen klicken.
Ob alles wie gewünscht funktioniert, seht ihr, indem ihr euren Smart-TV neustartet. Idealerweise sollte euch in dessen Menü jetzt keine Werbung mehr angezeigt werden.
Die Werbung im Heimnetz lässt sich schon lange mit einer Fritzbox blocken. Man darf nur nicht den DNS des Providers nutzen, sondern trägt einen DNS eines DNS services ein. Z.b den von dns.adguard.com. (94.140.14.14 und 15.15)
Die Einstellungen sind ein bisschen versteckt, aber wer suched der findet…
Es geht und ging noch viel länger bevor es adguard gab.
Einfach in die Filterliste die Adressen der Werbeserver eintragen.
Kann man sogar mit der Sniffer Funktion der Fritzbox vorher rausfinden.
Dann in die Blacklist die domains eintragen, den Fernseher dieser liste zuweisen und fertig.

articles.title: India does not have structural excess manufacturing capacity: Goyal at G20
articles.text:
India does not have structural excess manufacturing capacity: Goyal at G20
Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal said industrial capacity in itself is not the issue; however, distortions can arise where geographical concentration of production is driven by hidden subsidies and support.
Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal said India does not have structural excess manufacturing capacity in the sectors identified by the G20 Presidency, asserting that the country's manufacturing capacity serves both domestic and global needs.
The US holds the G20 Presidency in 2026.
He also said industrial capacity in itself is not the issue; however, distortions can arise where geographical concentration of production is driven by hidden subsidies and support.
The minister added that diversification of production and supply chains is a legitimate objective, but it cannot be used as a pretext for measures outside WTO (World Trade Organisation) rules or shifting the burden of adjustment onto developing countries, which must retain policy space to industrialise.
"India's manufacturing capacity serves its domestic and global needs and that, in the sectors identified by the G20 Presidency, India does not have structural excess capacity," Goyal said.
India shares the concern of several G20 members that trade-distorting support in some countries leads to dumping and predatory pricing, and it addresses such practices through evidence-based WTO measures, including anti-dumping and countervailing duties, he added.
These remarks are important as the Office of the United States Trade Representative (USTR) launched two separate Section 301 investigations on March 11 and 12, covering 60 economies over concerns related to forced labour and excess industrial capacity.
One probe on forced labour concluded, and a 10% duty was imposed on countries, including India. Final findings on the other probe are awaited.
The US has flagged excess capacity issues in sectors such as steel, textiles, aluminium, automobiles, batteries, cement, chemicals, electronics, energy goods, glass, machine tools, machinery, non-ferrous metals, paper, plastics, processed food and beverages, robotics, satellites, semiconductors, ships, solar modules, and transportation equipment.
"India shares the concern of many members that trade-distorting support in some economies leads to dumping and predatory pricing and addresses it through WTO (World Trade Organisation) measures such as anti-dumping and countervailing duties, based on evidence, which are open to judicial review," the commerce ministry, in a statement, quoted Goyal as saying.
India is the fastest-growing large economy in the world, with a domestic-demand-driven economy serving 1.4 billion people, and is building manufacturing value chains from design to finished goods as a trusted link in global supply chains, he said.
Goyal participated in the concluding day of the G20 Trade Ministers' Meeting in Milwaukee, Wisconsin, and spoke in sessions on structural excess capacity and production, updating the Most-Favoured-Nation principle, ending forced labour in global supply chains, and the closing session.
Speaking on ending forced labour in global supply chains, Goyal said India's commitment to forced labour elimination is absolute and unconditional.
Measures at the border must be based on specific and verifiable evidence rather than presumptions about entire countries, regions or sectors, and must respect due process and WTO rules, he added.
International Labour Organization (ILO) is the competent, universal and tripartite body for labour standards, he said.
India supports the objective of eliminating forced labour and voluntary exchange of good practices among G20 members, provided such cooperation does not involve monitoring of members, create new obligations or result in information being used as a basis for unilateral trade action.
On updating the Most-Favoured-Nation principle, the minister said India's trade with G20 members depends on a transparent, non-discriminatory and rules-based trading system.
Most-Favoured-Nation treatment is a key guarantee of this system, ensuring that the same terms apply to the smallest and largest trader.
He emphasised that consensus remains central to the WTO and that special and differential treatment must be preserved to enable developing countries to catch up with developed economies.
Goyal also called for restoration of the two-tier dispute settlement system.

articles.title: iPhone Duo : l'astuce inédite d'Apple pour rendre la pliure de l'écran invisible sur le long terme
articles.text:
La sortie de l’iPhone Duo mi-octobre approche à grands pas et chaque jour apporte son lot de nouvelles concernant le premier smartphone pliant d’Apple.
L’un des principaux axes de communication de la marque à la pomme pour cette nouvelle catégorie de produits repose évidemment sur l’écran pliant et sa pliure, présentée comme invisible.
La pliure apparente : un problème de physique
Il conviendra de le vérifier lors du test du produit chez 01net, mais, même si Apple est parvenu à réaliser cet exploit, l’expérience accumulée par ses concurrents démontre qu’à terme, même les pliures les plus invisibles finissent par apparaître. Le fait de plier et déplier sans cesse le smartphone finit par réduire cet avantage chez toutes les marques, jusqu’à parfois atteindre le stade ultime : une pliure visible en permanence, même lorsque l’écran est bien lumineux et placé en face de vous.
Cela s’explique facilement : pour obtenir un écran pliant, les constructeurs ne peuvent pas recourir au verre, trop rigide. Ils ont donc mis au point diverses couches appliquées sur la dalle OLED afin d’imiter les écrans traditionnels et leur robustesse, tout en masquant la pliure.
Une solution simple : proposer un filtre de remplacement
C’est là que réside la solution d’Apple pour maintenir une pliure invisible : pouvoir changer la couche supérieure. La démarche paraît plutôt maligne, puisque c’est elle qui accumule les traces d’usure, les micro-rayures, mais aussi les marques les plus visibles causées par des milliers de pliages et dépliages.
Dans une interview accordée au compte TikTok @angietutorials, Kate Bergeron, vice-présidente en charge de l’ingénierie matérielle, a livré cette information :
 « Le revêtement mat de l’écran est très efficace pour, disons, atténuer les traces de pliure. Mais il y a une couche de protection par-dessus, et nous avons mené un travail d’ingénierie considérable pour que celle-ci s’use le plus lentement possible et pour vous permettre de profiter au maximum des performances de cette couche. Elle est d’ailleurs remplaçable, ce qui est un véritable atout pour le client : vous pouvez retirer cette couche et en installer une nouvelle. »
On notera dans cette déclaration qu’Apple a semble-t-il tenté de jouer sur les deux tableaux : concevoir une couche supérieure qui tienne le plus longtemps possible, tout en offrant la possibilité de la remplacer.
Nous avons même une idée de ce que cela pourrait coûter, du moins pour les abonnés au service d’assurance de la marque, AppleCare. Un utilisateur de X (Twitter) a repéré que le remplacement coûterait 19 dollars en magasin. Impossible de connaître le montant en euros à ce stade, ni le prix d’une intervention hors AppleCare.
 👉🏻 Suivez l’actualité tech en temps réel : ajoutez 01net à vos sources sur Google, et abonnez-vous à notre canal WhatsApp.
Source : 9to5Mac

articles.title: Rocket Report: SpaceX completes launch triple-header; Rocket Lab nets big contract
articles.text:
A Falcon 9 rocket climbs into the sky to begin the Crew-13 mission to the International Space Station as a Falcon Heavy rocket awaits its launch window Thursday about 3.5 miles away at Kennedy Space Center, Florida.
Credit:
SpaceX
A Falcon 9 rocket climbs into the sky to begin the Crew-13 mission to the International Space Station as a Falcon Heavy rocket awaits its launch window Thursday about 3.5 miles away at Kennedy Space Center, Florida.
Credit:
SpaceX
This week, SpaceX celebrated the first orbital launch of its new Starship rocket. I’m not sure many people, at least those outside of SpaceX, expected it to take 14 flights of Starship before it technically reached low-Earth orbit, but Monday morning’s launch finally added that to SpaceX’s list of accomplishments with its new super-heavy rocket. Starship had gone 99 percent of the way to orbit before, only held back by safety concerns around the possibility of stranding the huge rocket in space.
What was most notable for SpaceX with this Starship flight was that it unlocked a massive growth potential for Starlink, with the first 26 of the network’s new-generation Starlink V3 satellites successfully deployed Monday.
As always, we welcome reader submissions, and if you don’t want to miss an issue, please subscribe using the box below (the form will not appear on AMP-enabled versions of the site). Each report will include information on small-, medium-, and heavy-lift rockets as well as a quick look ahead at the next three launches on the calendar.
Rocket Lab scores its biggest launch contract yet. Rocket Lab has signed what it calls its largest Electron launch service agreement to date, a 20-mission agreement with Synspective, Aviation Week & Space Technology reports. Synspective is a Japanese company with a growing fleet of radar Earth-imaging satellites. It is one of Rocket Lab’s most loyal customers, with the company’s light-class Electron rocket having launched 13 of Synspective’s StriX radar sats since 2020. The most recent Rocket Lab launch for Synspective occurred last Friday, September 25.
Dedicated launch … Rocket Lab’s Electron launch vehicle is sized for dedicated launches of payloads like Synspective’s StriX satellites. The latest agreement extends Synspective’s total bookings with Rocket Lab to 47 launches, including the 13 already flown. “Signing 20 launches in a single deal is a massive vote of confidence not just in Electron but in the launch cadence, mission reliability, and orbital precision that Rocket Lab consistently delivers,” Rocket Lab founder and CEO Peter Beck said in a statement.
Portuguese company acquires what’s left of Orbex. A Portuguese space technology business has snapped up the assets of Orbex, the Scottish rocket maker that collapsed earlier this year, the Scotsman reports. The buyer, Omnidea, plans to establish its UK operations at Orbex’s former manufacturing facility in Scotland, having agreed to a deal to acquire the assets and intellectual property (IP) of the defunct rocket developer. An initial team of ex-Orbex employees will join the business, with Omnidea planning to recruit further as the operation develops.
No Prime resurrection … Omnidea, once a partner of Orbex, says it plans to use its new Scotland base as a center for “structures development and fabrication” and as a “hub for flight and ground system electronics.” Omnidea is a supplier of propulsion, fluid control, avionics, and thermal management components in the European space industry, but the company is also exploring other markets. It looks like Orbex’s Prime rocket, which never ventured near a launch pad, is still dead.
Rocket Report
Keep up with the latest in space exploration and rocket launches.
Crew-13 launches toward ISS. A four-person crew rocketed into orbit Thursday from Cape Canaveral Space Force Station, Florida, heading for a six-month expedition on the International Space Station, Ars reports. Riding a Falcon 9 rocket and Dragon spacecraft, the four crew members departed from Space Launch Complex-40 at Cape Canaveral at 11:10 am EDT. Nine minutes later, they were in orbit to begin closing in on the space station for docking Thursday evening.
Some notes … This mission is nothing particularly new for SpaceX (it’s the company’s 21st human spaceflight launch). But it is noteworthy for a few reasons. The commander, Jessica Watkins, became the first Black woman to lead a mission into space. Her crewmate, Canadian astronaut Joshua Kutryk, went to space while he and his wife are expecting their third child later this year.
It’s rare, but astronauts have been off the planet for their child’s birth before. Most recently, NASA astronaut Randy Bresnik, set to command the Artemis III mission next year, was flying aboard the Space Shuttle Atlantis in 2009 when his wife gave birth to their daughter in Houston. This launch was delayed several weeks to fix a leaky valve on Dragon’s propulsion system, work that involved cutting out the suspect valve and welding in a new one, an unusual but apparently successful repair method.
Canadian company pursues medium-lift rocket. More countries are becoming interested in developing their own access to space, including those that have historically paid US companies to launch their satellites. Canada is no different, and the Trump administration’s seeming obsession with lobbing threats and tariffs across the northern border has only crystallized Canadian interest in sovereign access to space.
This spring, the Canadian government announced the first awards to three companies—NordSpace, Reaction Dynamics, and Canada Rocket Company—to support work on rockets with “light lift” capability. Now, one of these rocket developers, Canada Rocket Company, says it is skipping over the small launch segment and going straight to a more ambitious medium-lift rocket, Ars reports.
R-2 V2? … Canada Rocket Company is following the lead of several US launch providers in going for a bigger rocket. “The advice we got from having spoken with about 150 engineers, from the director of Starship engineering all the way down to some entry-level folks, is that you’re not going to be able to de-risk a rocket development program by building a smaller rocket,” said Hugh Kolias, chief executive of the Canada Rocket Company, in an interview with Ars.
The company’s R-2 rocket somewhat resembles SpaceX’s Falcon 9 in renderings, with nine engines and landing legs that signal a future path toward reuse of the first stage. It could carry up to 12.5 metric tons to low-Earth orbit. If all goes well, Kolias said, the company could be ready to launch by 2032.
SpaceX rideshare launch deploys 130 payloads. An artificial intelligence prototype from Google, a methane-tracker, pharmaceutical manufacturing labs, and more hitched a ride onboard a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket from Vandenberg Space Force Base, California, on Thursday afternoon, Spaceflight Now reports. The rideshare mission, known as Transporter-18, carried 130 payloads into a polar Sun-synchronous orbit. It was SpaceX’s second launch of the day, following the successful flight of NASA’s SpaceX Crew-13 mission from Florida a few hours earlier.
Bread and butter … Much of the growing ecosystem of commercial satellite startups sees SpaceX’s rideshare launches as key enablers to their businesses, offering relatively inexpensive access to space on a predictable schedule. These kinds of launches, at least on Falcon 9, will likely go away in a couple of years as SpaceX transitions to the much larger Starship rocket. But for now, a bevy of satellite companies continue relying on Falcon 9 launches. The customers on Transporter-18 ranged from tech powerhouses like Google to scrappy startups like Starfish Space, alongside top remote sensing companies such as Planet Labs and ICEYE.
Starship reaches new heights in low-Earth orbit. SpaceX’s Starship rocket thundered into the sky over South Texas early Monday. It was the 14th test flight of the world’s most powerful launch vehicle. This time, however, the rocket’s massive upper stage squeezed out some extra oomph from its Raptor engines and accelerated to orbital velocity, Ars reports.
On all of Starship’s previous flights, SpaceX intentionally dialed back the full capability of the rocket to fly a suborbital trajectory, slow enough for Earth’s gravity to pull the vehicle back into the atmosphere before it could complete a full lap around the planet. After several successful suborbital flights in a row, SpaceX officials decided this launch should go all the way to low-Earth orbit. And it did.
Debuting Starlink V3 … What’s more, SpaceX packed 26 of the company’s newest generation of Starlink broadband satellites into the rocket’s cargo bay. One by one, the flat-packed satellites—too large to fit inside SpaceX’s workhorse Falcon 9 rocket—were released from Starship’s payload deployer using a system of pulleys and cables to eject the satellites overboard like a Pez dispenser spits out candy. SpaceX cut a planned 10-hour test flight to three hours after one of the ship’s Raptor engines failed during ascent, but the vehicle was still able to make a pinpoint splashdown at one of its backup return sites north of Hawaii.
NASA will pay to human-rate ULA’s Vulcan rocket. NASA announced on Monday that it will exercise options to purchase two additional flights on Boeing’s Starliner spacecraft, as well as financially support the company in its efforts to return the crewed vehicle to flight and find a new rocket after the Atlas V vehicle retires, Ars reports. NASA is making the moves to preserve a path for its astronauts to low-Earth orbit as SpaceX nears retirement of its Falcon 9 rocket and Crew Dragon spacecraft. When that happens, Boeing’s troubled Starliner spacecraft will likely be the only commercial means of launching US crews to orbit.
A post-Atlas future … During a news conference on Monday, Dana Weigel, manager of NASA’s Low Earth Orbit Program, said the space agency would pay $359 million to Boeing to help the company complete a rebuild of the reaction control system thrusters that have overheated in flight. It would also certify United Launch Alliance’s Vulcan rocket for human missions. NASA also said it would exercise options to order two additional crewed missions on Starliner, bringing its total spaceflights on the vehicle to six. Any future Starliner flights beyond that would require a new rocket, like ULA’s Vulcan, as the Atlas V rocket is no longer in production.
SpaceX completes three launches in 13 hours. SpaceX pulled off two Falcon 9 rocket launches and a Falcon Heavy mission in less than 13 hours Thursday, marking one of the busiest days ever for the company’s launch teams. The action began, as noted previously in the Rocket Report, with a Falcon 9 launch from Cape Canaveral, Florida, carrying the next four-person crew to the International Space Station. A few hours later, another Falcon 9 lifted off from California on a rideshare mission. The launch of SpaceX’s triple-body Falcon Heavy rocket with a classified National Reconnaissance Office payload from Kennedy Space Center, Florida, rounded out the triple-header Thursday night.
And four landings … This was the first time a Falcon Heavy rocket has launched a payload for the NRO, the US government’s spy satellite agency. Little is publicly known about the payload except that it launched into a highly inclined orbit, flying northeast from Florida’s Space Coast. To add an extra flourish to the launch triple-header, SpaceX returned both Falcon 9 boosters to their launch sites in Florida and California and landed both side boosters from Falcon Heavy back at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station. That makes three launches and four landings (plus a Dragon docking at the ISS) in one day.
Blue Origin foresees growing launch cadence. As Blue Origin continues to recover from a New Glenn pad explosion in May, the company is seeking permission to significantly increase the vehicle’s launch rate, Space News reports. This is a big surprise, but a draft environmental assessment released this week puts some numbers to Blue Origin’s plans. The company is seeking permission from the FAA to increase the rate of New Glenn launches from Cape Canaveral Space Force Station’s Launch Complex 36 from 12 to 50 per year.
Reuse built in … The proposal would include 50 launches of the rocket and 50 landings of the rocket’s first stage on a drone ship in the Atlantic Ocean. It would also allow up to 100 static-fire tests, one for each stage of the rocket for each launch. The proposal also covers recovery of the rocket’s payload fairing, which Blue Origin has not attempted on any of the three launches of New Glenn to date.
Next three launches
October 5: Falcon 9 | SDA Tranche 1 Transport Layer A | Vandenberg Space Force Base, California | 08:17 UTC
October 7: KSLV-2 | NEONSAT 2-6 | Naro Space Center, South Korea | 03:23 UTC
October 9: Long March 12 | Unknown Payload | Wenchang Space Launch Site, China | 19:25 UTC
Stephen Clark is a space reporter at Ars Technica, covering private space companies and the world’s space agencies. Stephen writes about the nexus of technology, science, policy, and business on and off the planet.

articles.title: Sapphire Radeon RX 7000 Series Cards Get vBIOS Security Update
articles.text:
Friday, October 2nd 2026
Sapphire Radeon RX 7000 Series Cards Get vBIOS Security Update
AMD Radeon RX 7000 series RDNA 3 graphics cards today received a new vBIOS security update. According to AMD's add-in card partner Sapphire, the update is now available for Sapphire's own Radeon RX 7600, RX 7600 XT, RX 7650 GRE, RX 7700 XT, RX 7800 XT, RX 7900 GRE, RX 7900 XT, and RX 7900 XTX models. This update covers all the desktop graphics cards that AMD released for the RDNA 3 lineup and marks one of the rare occurrences of GPU vBIOS updates in recent times. Typically, these vBIOS updates are reserved for security patches, and Sapphire confirms that the company has been working to address a security issue identified in partnership with AMD.
Before updating the GPU firmware, ensure that the AMD Adrenalin Edition graphics driver is installed and that you have about 15-20 minutes to complete the update. To update the GPU firmware, Sapphire provides links to the specific GPU model affected. Once downloaded, run the updater as an administrator, choose a folder to save the executable files, and locate that folder. Once inside, run the program as an administrator again, and the AMD Radeon Firmware Updater tool will start. This tool will detect any AMD GPU present and indicate if there is a new firmware update. As shown in the example below, select the GPU and run the update, which will prompt a reboot once it is finished. Note that for the Radeon RX/PRO 7000 Series, the tool automatically runs twice: once in regular mode and a second time in safe mode to complete the process.After installation, confirm that the new GPU vBIOS firmware update is completed using the AMD Adrenalin software, which will display the exact firmware version installed on your graphics card. For reference on the installation process, follow Sapphire's installation guide step-by-step, though it should be fairly straightforward.
Source:

I do know about ucontroller, i was only reading a bit 01 / 2026 about it. the firmware blocks access to the hidden bus, which is when i am not wrong, a renamed i2c bus.
It's one of the reasons why they are so hesitant to push GPU firmware updates, and try to fix everything in software drivers. 99% of the time that's enough, but for example here, it isn't.
Lets hope XFX does the same for their models.
I still run a 6700XT and i'm "glad" it's one of the few generations that still works with MPT. You can easily increase the default 180W into a 300W card with clocks up to 2.8 ~ 2.9Ghz for quite the improvement.

articles.title: SpaceX faz viagem mais rápida de uma nave dos EUA até a Estação Espacial
articles.text:
A cápsula Dragon, da SpaceX, estabeleceu novo recorde ao realizar a viagem mais rápida de uma nave estadunidense até a Estação Espacial Internacional (ISS, na sigla em inglês). A espaçonave levou apenas 7 horas e 55 minutos entre o lançamento e o acoplamento ao laboratório orbital.
A Dragon, batizada de Grace, decolou na quinta-feira (1), às 12h10 (horário de Brasília), impulsionada por um foguete Falcon 9. O acoplamento ocorreu às 20h05, no módulo Harmony da ISS.
A missão Crew-13 transportou quatro astronautas: os americanos Jessica Watkins e Luke Delaney, o canadense Joshua Kutryk e o russo Serguei Teteriatnikov. O grupo permanecerá aproximadamente seis meses na estação, onde realizará pesquisas científicas, manutenção e demonstrações de tecnologias.
Recorde de velocidade até a ISS atingido pela SpaceX
- A NASA já havia planejado que a Crew-13 faria o trajeto em aproximadamente 7 horas e 50 minutos, duração que seria a mais rápida já registrada por uma nave estadunidense entre o lançamento e a chegada à estação. O tempo final ficou em 7 horas e 55 minutos;
- O tempo de viagem não significa que a Dragon tenha necessariamente atingido uma velocidade inédita. A diferença está principalmente na trajetória escolhida para alcançar a estação. Missões desse tipo precisam realizar uma série de manobras orbitais para sincronizar a nave com a ISS, que viaja ao redor da Terra a cerca de 28,2 mil km/h;
- A Dragon realizou o encontro com a estação de maneira autônoma e se conectou à porta voltada para o espaço do módulo Harmony;
- “A Crew-13 é mais uma demonstração da capacidade incomparável dos Estados Unidos em voos espaciais tripulados e da força de nossas parcerias comerciais”, afirmou Jared Isaacman, administrador da NASA;
- Segundo ele, os quatro astronautas darão continuidade ao trabalho científico na ISS e ajudarão a desenvolver a experiência e as capacidades necessárias para futuras missões à Lua e além.
Quem está a bordo
A comandante da missão é Jessica Watkins, astronauta da NASA que está em sua segunda viagem à estação espacial. Ela já havia passado 170 dias em órbita durante a missão Crew-4, em 2022.
Com a Crew-13, Watkins se tornou a primeira astronauta da NASA a realizar dois voos para a ISS a bordo de uma espaçonave Dragon da SpaceX. Antes de ingressar na NASA, ela estudou geologia e participou da equipe científica do rover Curiosity, que explora Marte.
O piloto da missão é Luke Delaney, em seu primeiro voo espacial. Ele é ex-aviador naval e piloto de testes, além de ter trabalhado como piloto de pesquisa no Centro de Pesquisa Langley, da NASA.
Também estreiam no espaço Joshua Kutryk, da Agência Espacial Canadense, e Serguei Teteriatnikov, da agência espacial russa Roscosmos.
Kutryk foi piloto de caça CF-18 e piloto de testes antes de ser selecionado como astronauta canadense. Já Teteriatnikov tem formação em engenharia naval e atuou em diferentes funções relacionadas à engenharia de sistemas de propulsão de embarcações.
Leia mais:
- Sonda que tem Júpiter como destino usa gravidade da Terra para mudar de rota e economizar combustível
- NASA prepara novo teste da Starliner após falhas no voo de 2024
- SpaceX lança chips de IA do Google ao espaço em teste para futuros data centers orbitais
Tripulação ficará seis meses em órbita
Durante a permanência na ISS, a Crew-13 participará de experimentos científicos e trabalhos de manutenção da estação. Entre os objetivos da missão estão pesquisas relacionadas à saúde dos astronautas, aos efeitos da microgravidade e a tecnologias que poderão ser utilizadas em futuras missões espaciais.
A chegada dos quatro astronautas também inicia a transição com a tripulação da missão Crew-12, que já está na estação.
A Crew-12 é formada pelos astronautas estadunidenses Jessica Meir e Jack Hathaway, pela astronauta francesa Sophie Adenot, da Agência Espacial Europeia (ESA, na sigla em inglês), e pelo cosmonauta russo Andrei Fediaiev. O grupo deve retornar à Terra a partir de segunda-feira (5), depois de alguns dias de transferência de responsabilidades entre as equipes.
Missão da SpaceX sofreu atraso antes do lançamento
A Crew-13 originalmente deveria ter chegado à estação antes, mas a missão sofreu adiamento provocado por um problema técnico identificado na cápsula.
O lançamento acabou ocorrendo em 1º de outubro, após a resolução do problema. Com o sucesso da missão, a Dragon completou o trajeto entre a Terra e a ISS em menos de oito horas, estabelecendo o novo recorde de lançamento até acoplamento de uma nave estadunidense na estação.
A ISS, por sua vez, continua recebendo tripulações de diferentes países. A presença conjunta de astronautas da NASA, da Agência Espacial Canadense, da ESA e da Roscosmos mantém a estação como uma das principais plataformas internacionais para pesquisas em microgravidade e operações espaciais de longa duração.
Rodrigo Mozelli é jornalista formado pela Universidade Metodista de São Paulo (UMESP) e, atualmente, é redator do Olhar Digital.

articles.title: Circuit Breaker Labs hopes to make AI safer for your kids (and you) | TechCrunch
articles.text:
With all the talk about how AI might one day kill us all, it’s easy to forget that AI has already been life-threatening to some, not through bioweapons, but psychologically.
For example, Character.AI settled several wrongful death lawsuits earlier this year brought by families of underage users who died by suicide after interactions with its bots. Multiple families have also sued OpenAI over ChatGPT’s alleged role in their loved ones’ suicides and delusions.
Making AI safer across languages and cultures is the mission of Circuit Breaker Labs, one of TechCrunch’s 2026 Startup Battlefield 200 finalists. (Circuit Breaker will be pitching at TechCrunch Disrupt, which takes place this year at Moscone West in San Francisco from October 13-15.)
Founders Shirali and Arul Nigam, who are siblings, were motivated by Sewell Setzer, the 14-year-old who developed an emotional attachment to a Character.AI chatbot and confessed thoughts to it of harming himself before dying by suicide. The chatbot, the parents alleged in a 2024 lawsuit, encouraged him. The bot may not have understood what words like “I want to be with you” really implied, said Arul, who is Circuit Breaker Labs’ CTO.
“A lot of people, especially young people, turn to these systems for support, and usually they aren’t actually getting the help they need. But in many cases, they’re actively being harmed, and people unfortunately have taken their lives already,” Arul said. “Those sorts of safety vulnerabilities, where people aren’t necessarily actively trying to break the system — they’re engaging in a natural way — and the system has context pollution or it doesn’t understand the nuance, and then takes really dangerous action, we’re trying to prevent that.”
Circuit Breaker Labs has created AI agents that it likens to an army of crash-test dummies. These agents mimic folks from all ages, backgrounds, languages, and cultures, and are used to test models on their ability to detect dangerous, psychologically harmful interactions.
“The way a six-year-old girl versus a 45-year-old man, or someone who speaks English as a first language versus a second language, or … gamer slang versus someone else who uses a different kind of slang, all of those can really trip up a model,” said Shirali, who is Circuit Breaker Labs’ CEO. “Models are really good at handling standard speech patterns, but nobody actually talks like that and so if the model misunderstands nuance or slang, it can go really badly.”
The startup works with human domain experts to build its hyper-realistic user simulations in order to run “red-team” tests against models, which are adversarial tests meant to uncover weaknesses. The tests are built to reflect real human speech patterns, slang, coded language, and typos. Circuit Breaker Labs then runs tens of thousands to hundreds of thousands of simulated interactions per day.
The idea is to ensure that a model can appropriately respond to risky interactions that may emerge over time and over many conversations. Circuit Breaker Labs then uses a proprietary scoring method to create auditable, explainable scores.
Circuit Breaker Labs is currently operating as an AI safety testing lab for high-risk AI applications such as AI coaching, journaling, or other mental health support apps, though Arul declined to name its marquee customers. Although the startup has a working product, it is in the very early stages, with only five employees, including the Nigam siblings.
Eventually, though, the testing platform could be applied to any app where someone may fall down an “AI psychosis” hole, where the human is at risk of developing a parasocial relationship with a chatbot. Examples include AI “co-worker” agents, whose responses can vary from one interaction to the next.
“People are becoming more skeptical of AI or more resistant to adopt it across the board,” Arul said, adding that while skepticism is healthy, banning a potentially valuable tool over safety concerns would be “regressive.”
Circuit Breakers Labs believes the answer to those fears is making AI safer. “We want to help build that trust for people.”
Come learn much more about Circuit Breaker Labs and many other innovative startups that have been vetted by TechCrunch at our Startup Battlefield competition, happening in downtown San Francisco on October 13-15.

articles.title: Apple endurece la seguridad de macOS para que la IA no acceda a tu información
articles.text:
Darle el control de tu ordenador a un agente de IA puede ser un arma de dos filos. Aunque las compañías afirman que sus modelos son seguros y tienen mecanismos de seguridad para evitar que accedan a tus archivos, la realidad es que pueden saltárselos sin que te des cuenta. Eso ocurrió con Muse, el agente de Meta que provocó que Apple lanzara una actualización para blindar los discos de Mac.
De acuerdo con TechCrunch, Apple anunció que endurecerá los controles de Acceso total al disco, el permiso que permite a una aplicación acceder a casi todo el contenido en macOS. La compañía publicó una actualización en su web para desarrolladores, señalando que el motivo de esta actualización obedece al auge de los agentes de IA.
“Algunos desarrolladores están utilizando el Acceso completo al disco de formas que podrían poner en riesgo a los usuarios, exponiendo todo en sus sistemas —incluidos archivos, correos, mensajes e incluso historial de navegación— sin que los usuarios tengan pleno conocimiento y comprensión”, mencionó Apple. “En aplicaciones de comunicación, esto también puede comprometer la privacidad de las personas con las que los usuarios se comunican”.
Aunque el control de Acceso total al disco se creó para que las copias de seguridad funcionaran correctamente, una app puede leer los archivos personales del usuario. Aplicaciones como Muse, el agente de IA de Meta, requieren ciertos permisos para poder controlar el ordenador y acceder a tus documentos. Estos agentes pueden salirse de control, por lo que Apple no quiso arriesgarse y confirmó que los permisos se otorgarán solo con el consentimiento explícito del usuario.
Muse para Mac accedió a los mensajes de un usuario sin su permiso
La decisión de Apple tiene que ver con un incidente que ocurrió con el agente de Meta. Hace unos días, el periodista Jason Aten reveló que Muse accedió al contenido de sus mensajes sin que él le diera permiso. Aten descubrió que la IA sincronizaba la base de datos local de mensajes de su Mac, pero al cuestionar al agente, este dijo solo recibía el texto de las notificaciones que aparecían en el escritorio.
Muse funciona sobre una máquina virtual segura con 8 GB de memoria y 8 GB de almacenamiento que Meta ofrece gratis. Según la tecnológica, esto garantiza la privacidad del usuario y que no se accederá a datos e información personal si no tiene autorización. Pero Muse se delató al sugerir a Aten que convirtiera una de sus conversaciones de iMessage en una columna, algo que nunca debió haber pasado.
A este incidente se suma otro con ChatGPT para Mac, en el cual un fallo en la app podría haber permitido a atacantes acceder a datos sensibles. De acuerdo con el reporte de Wired, expertos de seguridad encontraron una vulnerabilidad en la app de OpenAI, que abría la puerta para que un hacker leyera tu historial de conversaciones con la IA y otros archivos almacenados en la app, incluidas las sesiones de navegador.
“A medida que los agentes de IA se vuelven cada vez más capaces y autónomos, los riesgos asociados a este nivel de acceso crecerán considerablemente”, mencionó Apple.

articles.title: GitHub's advice for its new Copilot feature is to try something else first
articles.text:
GitHub’s advice for its new Copilot feature is to try something else first
GitHub launched computer use in public preview on Thursday, giving Copilot CLI and its desktop app the ability to operate applications on macOS and Windows. Agents can read app content and click, type, scroll, and drag, including in older, GUI-only software with no API, command-line interface, or MCP integration.
An expense report in Safari was GitHub’s launch demonstration but the company described other uses including summarizing information in a legacy application, updating a presentation, entering data, and moving information between apps. Developers can access the feature from the terminal or through the Copilot app, which runs on Copilot CLI and launched earlier this year as a rival to Claude Code and Codex.
GitHub has some catching up to do. OpenAI added computer use to Codex in April, while Anthropic brought broader computer use on macOS to Claude Code and Claude Cowork earlier this year.
GitHub has some catching up to do.
Computer use vs. MCP servers
Enabling computer use in Copilot CLI activates a bundled plugin with its own MCP server. It works in local sessions, reading application content through the operating system’s accessibility tree and taking screenshots when it needs visual context.
The company recommends using direct tools wherever possible. So, if an API, MCP server, terminal command, filesystem tool, or dedicated browser tool can handle the task, it typically provides more structured information and more predictable results than desktop interaction.
That advice limits where GitHub thinks computer use belongs. OpenAI president Greg Brockman made a broader case last month, arguing that agents could use the same interfaces as people and spare the industry the work of building and maintaining a connector for every piece of software.
Saved approvals outlast their removal
Developers enable the feature with /computer on in Copilot CLI or through the Copilot app’s Computer Use settings. macOS also requires Accessibility permission to operate controls and Screen Recording permission to inspect windows when visual context is needed.
The CLI session’s permission mode determines whether Copilot asks before accessing an app; developers can check it with /permissions show. When prompted, they can allow access for the current session, choose “Always allow” for future sessions or decline. Deny rules override both automatic and saved approvals.
Approvals saved in the CLI carry over to the desktop app on the same computer. Removing an app from the always-allowed list clears its approval for future sessions but leaves access already granted in a running session intact.
Stopping work requires a separate action: press Esc twice in the CLI, or click Stop or press Esc in the desktop app.
Enterprise controls over computer use
Enterprise policy overrides a developer’s local preference. If managed settings block computer use, Copilot CLI reports that the feature is unavailable.
Enterprise policy overrides a developer’s local preference.
Through managed-settings.json, enterprise owners can also control whether developers may bypass approval prompts. That restriction applies across the Copilot app, CLI, and VS Code.
GitHub’s default-enablement policy for Business and Enterprise does not change this preview’s opt-in status. The policy starts applying to unconfigured features on October 22 but excludes preview features.
Reliability depends on the interface
A change in timing or window state can cause Copilot to repeat an action or stall. GitHub also warns that the agent may choose the wrong control, type into the wrong field, or struggle with dynamic interfaces and complex workflows.
Sensitive information visible in an application window may also become context for the agent.
Unexpected on-screen content and ambiguous instructions can lead to actions affecting the user’s device, data, or connected accounts. Sensitive information visible in an application window may also become context for the agent.

articles.title: GitLab warns of critical RCE vulnerability in AI Gateway service
articles.text:
GitLab warned customers today to immediately patch a critical AI Gateway vulnerability that could let attackers run arbitrary commands on vulnerable instances.
AI Gateway is a service that gives access to AI-native GitLab Duo features. While GitLab operates its own cloud-based AI Gateway instance used by GitLab.com, GitLab Self-Managed, and GitLab Dedicated, users can also deploy their own self-hosted instances on GitLab Self-Managed through GitLab Duo Self-Hosted.
Tracked as CVE-2026-90970, this security flaw stems from an improper neutralization weakness and can let attackers with basic privileges and Duo Agent Platform access execute arbitrary commands on unpatched instances.
"GitLab has remediated an issue in the GitLab AI Gateway that, under certain conditions, could have allowed an authenticated user with Duo Agent Platform access to escape the prompt template sandbox via a specially crafted flow configuration, leading to arbitrary command execution on the AI Gateway," the company explained in a Friday advisory.
GitLab released versions 19.2.4, 19.3.2, and 19.4.1 to address this vulnerability for Self-Hosted AI Gateway users and said that customers using a GitLab-hosted AI Gateway are already protected and do not need to take action.
"These versions contain a critical security fix for GitLab Self-Hosted AI Gateway, and we strongly recommend that all GitLab Self-Managed customers with GitLab Self-Hosted AI Gateway installations update to one of these versions immediately," it said. "We have conducted targeted outreach to Self-Hosted AI Gateway customers prior to this release post with this guidance."
GitLab added that it reached out to those who host their own AI Gateway before disclosure and urged users to upgrade vulnerable instances as soon as possible.
Last month, GitLab also patched a maximum severity path traversal vulnerability (CVE-2026-85706) in GitLab Community Edition (CE) and Enterprise Edition (EE) that allows unauthenticated attackers to read sensitive data such as credentials and other secrets from vulnerable servers.
One day later, the U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) added CVE-2026-85706 to its list of actively exploited flaws and gave federal agencies three days to secure their systems as mandated by Binding Operational Directive (BOD) 26-04.
Since November 2021, CISA has tagged five GitLab vulnerabilities abused in the wild, including one exploited by ransomware gangs.
GitLab's DevSecOps platform has over 30 million registered users and is used by over 50% of Fortune 100 companies, including Nvidia, Lockheed Martin, T-Mobile, Goldman Sachs, Airbus, and UBS.

articles.title: Meta’s AI could flood the internet; Four Indian brands putting a new spin on khadi
articles.text:
Meta’s AI could flood the internet; Four Indian brands putting a new spin on khadi
A new report on Meta’s latest AI developments explores how the company’s push could accelerate the creation of machine-generated content at a scale that changes what we see—and trust—online.
Dear Reader,
AI is moving deeper into the systems around us—from research labs and universities to cybersecurity and the very fabric of the internet.
The web could be entering a new AI-heavy era. A new report on Meta’s latest AI developments explores how the company’s push could accelerate the creation of machine-generated content at a scale that changes what we see—and trust—online. The prospect raises bigger questions about how the internet will evolve as AI-generated material becomes increasingly difficult to distinguish from human-created content.
But the AI race is also creating new targets for cyber espionage. Chinese hackers reportedly impersonated a former US official to target AI experts, seeking access to emails and other information. The campaign highlights how AI expertise itself has become a valuable target as countries and organisations compete for technological advantage.
Meanwhile, IBM is deepening its academic AI partnerships in India, expanding collaborations with IIT Bombay and IISc. The work spans areas including agentic AI, Indic-language and sovereign AI, multimodal systems and AI infrastructure, bringing industry and academia closer together as India builds its AI research capabilities.
In other news, Seeds Fincap has raised more than Rs 100 crore in a Series B round led by the Michael & Susan Dell Foundation. The NBFC plans to use the capital to expand its branch network, hire field teams and strengthen its risk-tracking capabilities as it targets Rs 1,000 crore in assets under management by March 2027.
In today’s newsletter, we will talk about
- Four Indian brands putting a new spin on khadi
- How Prableen Kaur Gill became Asia’s No. 1 street lifter
Here’s your trivia for today: What was the name of the first computer virus? (Scroll down for the answer)
Sustainability
Four Indian brands putting a new spin on khadi
Khadi is moving beyond its traditional image, with a new generation of entrepreneurs bringing technology, contemporary design and sustainable practices to the handspun fabric. These four Indian brands are finding new ways to make khadi relevant to modern consumers while supporting artisans and rural communities.
Key takeaways:
- Greenwear is using solar-powered charkhas, looms and sewing machines, while creating a decentralised production network involving rural women and artisans.
- Retiyo and Weavers Stores are bringing khadi into everyday wardrobes with modern silhouettes, versatile designs and lifestyle products.
- Tula takes a value-chain approach, working with organic indigenous cotton, handspinning, handweaving and natural dyes while focusing on farmers and artisans.
Story
How Prableen Kaur Gill became Asia’s No. 1 street lifter
From struggling to do a single pull-up to becoming Asia’s No. 1 street lifter, Prableen Kaur Gill’s journey is one of discipline, setbacks and relentless self-belief. Today, she is using her story to encourage more women to discover their strength.
Key takeaways:
- Prableen started callisthenics when she was unable to complete a single pull-up. She went on to compete internationally and set a national record in the muscle-up.
- Injuries, including one that required ankle surgery, tested her physically and mentally, but she continued to train and compete.
- What began as a personal fitness diary on Instagram has grown into a community of more than 200,000, with Prableen now focused on getting more women into strength sports.

- Security cameras: Amazon and Walmart-owned Flipkart are reviewing security camera listings in India after hundreds of unlicensed products were found on their platforms, despite government testing rules introduced six months ago amid espionage concerns.
- Gemini 4 Argon: Google parent Alphabet has launched Gemini 4 Argon, a new AI model built to handle tasks such as coding, research and writing. Google says the model has a particular strength in cybersecurity.

articles.title: SFR prépare la Box 10, une nouvelle box Internet moins chère, mais avec quelques concessions
articles.text:
En juillet 2025, SFR a dévoilé la Box 10+, une box internet fibre compatible Wi-Fi 7, au prix de 44,99 €. Aujourd’hui, un peu plus d’un an plus tard donc, des pages d’assistance nous révèlent l’existence d’une nouvelle box chez SFR : la Box 10 (sans le petit « + »). Celle-ci se veut plus abordable financièrement, mais elle fait par conséquent aussi quelques concessions par rapport à son prédécesseur. Attention, la Box 10 n’a pas encore été dévoilée officiellement par l’opérateur téléphonique, mais sa présentation, et dans la foulée sa commercialisation, devraient être imminentes. Quoi qu’il en soit, voici ses principales caractéristiques.
Une Box plus abordable, mais qui fait certaines concessions de performance
Au niveau du design, la Box 10 reprend quasiment les mêmes formes que la Box 10+. Nous retrouvons ainsi deux façades noires et un petit écran E-Ink sur la tranche, qui indique différentes informations : la connexion Internet, le réseau Wi-Fi, le téléphone fixe et le mode économie d’énergie. En parlant d’énergie, sa consommation électrique s’élève à 9,4 W. On retrouve bien entendu un bouton d’allumage ON/OFF et un bouton RESET, ainsi qu’un connecteur d’alimentation électrique.
Niveau connectique, la Box 10 présente un port TEL RJ45, deux ports 2,5 Gigabit Ethernet (GE), deux ports 1 GE, un port USB-C et un connecteur pour fibre optique (technologie GPON).
La Box 10 se contente donc de la norme GPON, ce qui lui permet de gérer des abonnements allant jusqu’à 2 Gb/s. À titre de comparaison, la Box 10+ bénéficie d’un port 10 Gb/s, ainsi que du XGS-PON, lui permettant de prendre en charge des débits jusqu’à 8 Gb/s. Pour le sans-fil, la Box 10 se limite au Wi-Fi 7 sur les bandes 2,4 et 5 GHz. La Box 10+ ajoute quant à elle la bande 6 GHz, ce qui lui permet d’atteindre des débits supérieurs à courte distance.
Quand la Box 10 pourrait-elle être disponible ?
Comme nous l’avons déjà précisé, SFR n’a pas encore officiellement dévoilé la Box 10. La Box 10+ avait été présentée en juillet 2025, avant d’être proposée à certains clients les plus fidèles dès le mois d’août. Son lancement avait ensuite été généralisé en septembre 2025. Il est donc possible que la Box 10 suive un calendrier similaire. Il ne reste désormais plus qu’à attendre une communication officielle de la part de SFR.

articles.title: Crypto Scammers Hijack Microsoft’s Official X Account
articles.text:
Microsoft has confirmed that its official X account was taken over on Thursday and used to amplify a Clippy-themed cryptocurrency account.
According to The Verge, the company’s account, which has more than 13 million followers, started following the crypto account and shared one of its messages. Microsoft’s profile picture was also replaced with an image of Clippy, the animated paperclip assistant that shipped with older versions of Office.
The account behind the reposted message, @clippymsftcto, posed as Clippy and has since been suspended. A second account involved in the incident kept pushing a $Clippy token, saying its liquidity pool was paired with $MSFT.
The posts were eventually taken down. According to The Verge, an apology appeared on the Microsoft account roughly 30 minutes later and was deleted soon after, with no explanation given.
The now-deleted post said Microsoft was aware of a token being marketed in connection with its stock that used the Clippy brand without permission. “To be clear, Microsoft does not support, endorse, sponsor, or authorize any cryptocurrency or crypto-related token,” it read.
A Microsoft spokesperson told The Verge, “We have confirmed unauthorized access to our account on X, including posts that did not come from Microsoft,” adding, “The account has been secured and the unauthorized posts have been removed, and we are continuing to investigate the circumstances.”
Microsoft has not said how the attackers gained access to its account, and hackers have several options beyond tricking a social media manager into entering their credentials on a phishing page.
They can take over the phone number tied to the account through SIM swapping, as it happened with the SEC’s X account in 2024, or hijack the email address used for password resets.
Infostealer malware on an employee’s device can also steal browser session cookies from an active login, letting attackers access the account without a password or an MFA prompt. Another route is a compromised third-party marketing or social media management tool that has been authorized to post on the company’s behalf.

articles.title: 39 years in tech, one hard lesson: Lungi Sangqu on why buying software won't fix broken processes - TechCabal
articles.text:
Thirty-nine years ago, Lungi Sangqu wrote her first lines of code. Nearly four decades later—after shaping digital systems across 49 African countries in banking, rail, logistics, and higher education—her most profound lesson has nothing to do with software. For this week’s Coffee With…, PHATHISANI MOYO sits down with the founder and CEO of Africa Digital Success to discuss why millions in enterprise tech spending go to waste, why C-suites must stop delegating strategy solely to IT departments, and what these years in computing teach us about AI and the human element of work.
In 1987, Lungi Sangqu discovered computer science and became captivated by its capacity to solve complex problems at speed. At the time, computing remained a novelty to most people in her community, but for Sangqu, it provided a clear window into tomorrow.
“I knew that I was learning about the future,” she told TechCabal.
Nearly four decades later, as the founder and chief executive officer (CEO) of Africa Digital Success, a pan-African digital transformation consultancy, Sangqu has spent her career helping institutions navigate that very future. Her work has spanned government, banking, education, logistics, and rail infrastructure across South Africa and the wider continent.
Yet her most profound insight has little to do with code or hardware. Technology can execute flawlessly according to specification and still fail the human beings expected to adopt it. The dividing line between success and failure, Sangqu has learnt, rests on leadership decisions, human-centric system design, and whether executives truly comprehend the problem they are attempting to solve.
A curiosity that began in Mthatha
Sangqu was raised in Mthatha, in South Africa’s Eastern Cape Province, attending Ross Primary School before completing her matriculation at Ngangelizwe High School. She subsequently pursued university studies in mathematics, chemistry, and computer science.
Computer science captured her imagination in 1987. Intrigued by the sheer speed with which algorithms could resolve complex calculations, she advanced through Computer Science III.
While her early technical grounding laid the foundation for her career, decades of practical application broadened her perspective on technology’s ultimate purpose.
“Mathematics taught me discipline; technology taught me possibility; working in institutions taught me that both must be placed in service of people,” she reflects.
Starting as a software programmer in the early 1990s, Sangqu developed a sharp eye for detail and a deep appreciation for the operational staff who keep systems running. As she transitioned into larger institutions, the core challenges grew increasingly complex.
The fundamental questions evolved beyond technical functionality. Instead, they centered on strategic alignment: Why did the organisation require this system? Who would operate it? What was the true cost-to-benefit ratio? Would it measurably improve service delivery?
“As I moved into larger organisations, I saw that the hardest technology problems often sat outside the code,” she explains.
Her career trajectory took her through high-stakes roles at the Public Service Commission, the Department of Social Development, the State Information Technology Agency (SITA), the South African Post Office, the South African Reserve Bank, DHL Express, the University of South Africa (UNISA), Walter Sisulu University, and Transnet Freight Rail.
At DHL, her operational scope spanned 49 African countries. Across these diverse environments, Sangqu observed a universal truth: organisations must always start with the problem, never the product.
“Every problem requires the right technology,” she emphasises.
Transforming South Africa’s largest distance learning institution
A defining example of this philosophy occurred during her tenure at UNISA, South Africa’s largest open-distance learning institution. Sangqu led initiatives to digitise student applications, registration, assignment submission, and grading workflows.
This was not merely an IT procurement exercise. The university had to re-engineer core processes, train administrative staff, and evaluate whether digital tools served the institution’s educational mandate. By August 2013, UNISA had successfully transitioned assignment marking fully online.
However, the transition highlighted crucial equity considerations. Students required compatible devices and reliable broadband. While digital workflows streamlined operations for urban learners, they created friction for rural students lacking internet access.
For Sangqu, this underscores why digital initiatives cannot be evaluated solely by launch milestones.
“A successful launch is only a milestone,” she notes. “The real test is whether the organisation can sustain the change and whether the people it serves experience a tangible improvement.”
Addressing the governance and leadership deficit
After decades within major public and private enterprises, Sangqu grew troubled by how institutions evaluated digital investments. Too often, executive boards celebrated the acquisition of expensive platforms rather than improvements in customer experience, staff productivity, or decision-making quality.
She frequently witnessed organisations pouring millions into software without establishing a clear link to operational efficiency or revenue growth. In many instances, technology was brought into executive discussions as an afterthought—long after business strategy had been set.
To bridge this gap, Sangqu founded Africa Digital Success. The consultancy provides executive-level advisory services, helping leadership teams navigate technology risk, upskill talent, and execute sustainable digital strategies.
“The core gap was this,” she states. “Organisations were measuring technology by the wrong metrics, counting the platforms they acquired rather than asking whether technology helped them serve customers and citizens better.”
The habits that hold organisations back
One of the most persistent problems, she says, is the belief that technology belongs to the information technology (IT) department and that other executives need not concern themselves with it.
That separation can leave technology teams responsible for decisions they cannot make alone. A new system may require changes to budgets, staffing, customer service or everyday working practices. Without support from senior leaders, even a well-designed project can struggle.
Other habits create similar problems. Some organisations treat technology mainly as a cost to be reduced. Others assume an expensive international product must be better than a locally developed alternative. Departments may also keep information to themselves, making it harder for colleagues to see the full picture.
Slow approval processes can push employees to find their own solutions. A team unable to get permission for a digital tool may buy software independently or store information outside approved systems. Although this may help solve an immediate problem, it can leave the organisation exposed to security risks and unable to manage its information properly.
“Shadow IT is a governance and trust problem,” Sangqu said.
Her answer is not simply to impose more rules. Leaders need to take responsibility for technology decisions, while making internal processes clear and practical enough for employees to follow.
She also wants organisations to assess local technology on its merits rather than dismissing it before testing it. Products should be judged on whether they are reliable, secure, affordable and suitable for the organisation’s needs, not on where they come from or how familiar the supplier’s name is.
When organisations work with local providers, they can also create opportunities for skills development and knowledge transfer. Buying a system should not leave an organisation permanently dependent on an outside supplier.
AI, youth talent, and building enduring workplaces
These governance principles have become urgent as artificial intelligence reshapes the workplace. Sangqu advises boards to define the specific operational problem before deploying AI, verify data integrity, and establish clear human oversight.
Furthermore, leaders must plan for workforce transitions when tasks are automated—re-skilling employees for higher-value roles rather than viewing automation solely through a cost-reduction lens.
She sees a similar mandate regarding young professionals entering the workforce. Many arrive with native digital literacy, only to be stifled by manual workflows and risk-averse managers who value physical presenteeism over output.
“We cannot ask young professionals to innovate while requiring them to spend their days repairing avoidable gaps in legacy systems,” she remarks.
While institutional history and senior mentorship remain vital, Sangqu stresses that knowledge exchange must be reciprocal. Established leaders must listen to younger staff who can spot operational inefficiencies.
From writing raw code in 1987 to advising enterprise boards today, Sangqu’s career reflects a singular conviction: digital progress is measured by what it enables human beings to achieve.
Through Africa Digital Success, her goal is to build self-sustaining institutional capacity across the continent.
“I want younger Africans to inherit workplaces where their ideas can seamlessly become meaningful, impactful work,” she reflects.
For a pioneer whose journey began with the promise of computer logic nearly 40 years ago, Sangqu’s ultimate focus remains squarely on the human beings behind the machine.
True scale demands moving beyond surface-level integrations to robust execution. We’ve filtered the noise out of Moonshot 2026, optimising the conference strictly for high-calibre connections between startup founders, global financial operators, enterprise leaders and individuals rewiring Africa’s technical frameworks. articles.title: CyberGhost à 2,19 € par mois : le VPN numéro 1 selon Clubic est très abordable en ce moment
articles.text:
Il n’est pas nécessaire de dépenser une fortune pour se doter d’un VPN de qualité : CyberGhost VPN le démontre en proposant une formule donnant accès à 26 mois de protection pour 2,19 € par mois. Une promotion intéressante pour découvrir le service classé en tête du comparatif 2026 de Clubic.
Si l’intérêt des VPN pour la sécurité et la confidentialité des connexions à Internet est désormais connu, il peut encore être compliqué de
faire son choix entre les différents services au moment de s’abonner. Que
faut-il privilégier ? Les performances ? Les fonctionnalités ? Le nombre
d’appareils que l’on peut connecter simultanément ?
CyberGhost VPN a fait le choix d’adopter une approche destinée à un public aussi large que possible. Ce service est accessible par le biais d’applications disponibles sur de nombreuses plateformes, et il s’utilise sans connaissance technique particulière. Une promotion très intéressante est actuellement en cours sur le site de l’éditeur.
Une réduction de 82 % sur l’abonnement de 24 mois + 2 mois offerts
Pendant une durée limitée, CyberGhost VPN propose sa formule de deux ans avec deux mois supplémentaires offerts au prix de 2,19 € par mois, contre 11,99 € pour l’abonnement mensuel de référence. Précision importante : le montant correspondant aux 26 mois d’abonnement est facturé en une seule fois, soit 56,94 €.
La formule est assortie d’une garantie satisfait ou remboursé de 45 jours : durant cette période, vous pouvez tester tous les aspects du service sur les plateformes de votre choix, afin de vous assurer qu’il répond parfaitement à vos besoins avant de conserver l’abonnement.
CyberGhost VPN, un choix cohérent pour une famille
La polyvalence de CyberGhost VPN, associée à sa facilité d’utilisation, explique en grande partie pourquoi il occupe actuellement la première place du comparatif des meilleurs VPN de Clubic, avec une note de 9,8 sur 10.
CyberGhost peut protéger jusqu’à sept appareils simultanément. Ses applications couvrent les principales plateformes, dont Windows, macOS, Linux, Android et iOS, mais aussi différents téléviseurs et boîtiers multimédias. Une configuration sur certains routeurs est également possible pour étendre la protection à d’autres appareils du foyer.
Cela signifie qu’il est possible d’utiliser le service sur le téléviseur du salon, les ordinateurs de la maison, mais aussi les smartphones et tablettes de plusieurs membres de la famille. L’interface des différentes applications se montre très accessible : vous pouvez opter pour une connexion rapide ou choisir l’un des serveurs proposés dans 100 pays différents.
Certains serveurs sont optimisés pour le streaming ou pour le jeu en ligne, par exemple. Lors d’un séjour à l’étranger, une connexion à un serveur français peut notamment vous permettre de retrouver vos services habituels, sous réserve des conditions d’utilisation de chaque plateforme.
Le service prend en charge les protocoles WireGuard, OpenVPN et IKEv2. Il intègre également un kill Switch : si la connexion au VPN est interrompue, le trafic Internet peut être coupé afin d’éviter une exposition involontaire de l’adresse IP.
Pourquoi CyberGhost VPN occupe-t-il la première place chez Clubic ?
Pour connaître l’avis complet de Clubic concernant CyberGhost VPN, l’idéal reste de consulter son test. Dans les grandes lignes, celui-ci souligne la facilité d’utilisation des applications, des performances adaptées aux usages courants et un réseau couvrant une centaine de pays.
Sa politique d’absence de journaux d’activité, ses serveurs fonctionnant en mémoire vive et ses DNS privés constituent également des atouts en matière de confidentialité.
CyberGhost VPN se présente donc comme un service de choix pour les utilisateurs grand public en quête d’une solution accessible, équilibrée et dotée d’un bon rapport qualité-prix. Et c’est clairement le cas en ce moment avec la promotion en cours.
- storage11500 serveurs
- language100 pays couverts
- lan7 connexions simultanées
- moodEssai gratuit 45 jours
- thumb_upAvantage : meilleur équilibre prix/performance
CyberGhost convient au grand public grâce à sa prise en main facile, ses performances en streaming et P2P, et ses abonnements longue durée avantageux.
La transparence de CyberGhost s’est améliorée, mais son forfait mensuel reste moins intéressant, avec des fonctionnalités variables selon les plateformes et des options avancées parfois peu intuitives.
- Interface claire et agréable
- Très bon rapport qualité-prix sur la durée
- Streaming et P2P bien pris en charge

articles.title: Écran 16 pouces, nouvelles jantes et V2L : la Tesla Model 3 progresse en Chine, la France est prochaine sur la liste
articles.text:
Tesla a mis à jour sa Model 3 en Chine ce jeudi 1er octobre. La marque l’a annoncé avec quatre affiches publiées sur ses comptes officiels chinois, comme Weibo, et a mis à jour son site commercial. Toutes les versions de la berline reçoivent notamment un écran central plus grand et peuvent maintenant alimenter des appareils électriques. Voici toutes les nouveautés en détail.
Les évolutions du Model Y pour la Model 3
Le Model Y a reçu le même écran en janvier. La diagonale de la dalle passe de 15,4 à 16 pouces, tandis que Tesla promet une meilleure définition et un rafraîchissement plus rapide, sans donner de chiffres. La définition est en hausse également : QHD (2560 × 1440 pixels), contre 1920 × 1200 pour l’ancien écran.
Toutes les Model 3 et Model Y vendues en Chine peuvent désormais fournir jusqu’à 2,2 kW de puissance électrique, grâce au fameux V2L (vehicle-to-load), qui transforme la voiture en batterie portable géante via un adaptateur branché sur le port de charge. Tesla vend cet adaptateur 599 yuans en Chine, soit environ 80 €.
D’autres nouveautés touchent à l’apparence de la berline électrique. À l’intérieur, le ciel de toit en tissu passe du gris au noir, comme sur le Model Y. L’option de l’intérieur blanc disparaît au profit d’une sellerie baptisée « Gris Zen », déjà proposée sur le Model Y. Enfin, les jantes optionnelles Nova de 19 pouces sont plus foncées et prennent l’appellation « Dark Nova ».
Une partie de ces évolutions a suivi le lendemain aux États-Unis. Tesla North America a annoncé sur X que toutes les Model 3 vendues aux États-Unis, à Porto Rico et au Mexique adoptaient l’écran 16 pouces. La version Performance monte à 528 hp (environ 535 ch), contre 510 hp (environ 517 ch) à son lancement en 2024, et son autonomie EPA passe de 309 à 316 miles (de 497 à 509 km). En revanche, la Model 3 américaine n’a toujours pas droit au V2L, que Tesla réserve depuis août au Model Y Premium, au Model Y Performance et au Cybertruck aux États-Unis. L’intérieur gris n’y est pas proposé non plus, et le ciel de toit noir est réservé à la version Performance.
Pas avant novembre en France ?
Si Tesla n’a rien dit pour l’Europe, plusieurs indices vont tout de même dans le sens d’une arrivée rapide. D’après un message de Tesla Corée sur X, les Model 3 produites à Shanghai à partir d’octobre 2026 reçoivent toutes ces nouveautés. La Chine, la Corée du Sud, l’Australie et la Nouvelle-Zélande les ont déjà. Or, cette même Gigafactory chinoise produit également la Model 3 vendue en Europe.
Afin de connaître la potentielle date d’arrivée, il faut compter le trajet en bateau. Un cargo met plus d’un mois pour relier Shanghai à l’Europe. Les premières Model 3 mises à jour arriveraient donc chez les clients européens début novembre au plus tôt.
Si vous commandez une Model 3 en ce moment, demandez à Tesla à quelle date votre voiture sera fabriquée et vous saurez si vous profiterez de ces évolutions.
