articles.title: AutoSens 2026: Regulation Drives Automotive Sensing Architectures- EE Times
articles.text:
BARCELONA, Spain — At AutoSens and InCabin Europe 2026 in Barcelona, more than 1,000 engineers, executives, and semiconductor experts gathered to examine how evolving safety, perception, and computing requirements are influencing automotive sensor design.
OEMs and Tier-1 suppliers are working together, connecting chipmakers with automotive architects. Driving this development is a wave of regulations, especially Europe’s Euro NCAP 2026 protocols, which require carmakers to go beyond conventional parts.
Euro NCAP 2026 and in-cabin safety requirements
Euro NCAP’s 2026 safety protocols put greater emphasis on driver and occupant monitoring. Driver state monitoring (DSM) is a key part of the safe driving assessment. The protocols also assess child presence detection and award additional points for systems that can detect impairment and respond when a driver becomes unresponsive.
Camera-based systems can struggle when occupants or objects are obscured, such as a baby under a blanket or sleeping in a footwell. To address these limitations without raising costs, some suppliers are combining cameras with RF sensing technologies such as UWB and mmWave radar.
At AutoSens Europe 2026, Calterah demonstrated its Dubhe CAL1106AQ SoC, which the company stated is the first implementation of IEEE 802.15.4ab sensing in a FiRa 4.0-certified 2T4R UWB chip. With its Radar Leakage Suppression module, Calterah said the chip can detect tiny movements, such as the chest of a breathing infant, without a separate mmWave radar unit.
Calterah stated that its Bluetooth Low Energy-assisted multi-millisecond system can measure distances over 400 meters, even through parked cars. The company said the UWB upgrade can support child presence detection by updating existing keyless entry hardware with new software, which could make dedicated 60 GHz mmWave interior radars less necessary.
Meanwhile, Infineon Technologies showcased its XENSIV 60 GHz radar evaluation modules, demonstrating full-cabin monitoring and real-time radar point cloud overlays on live video feeds.
Advanced optical vision
Even with new RF technologies that can sense movement through obstacles, optical cameras are still essential for capturing detailed information inside the car.
Optical cameras can identify who is in the car, check where people are looking to see if they are distracted, and read small facial expressions to spot fatigue.
At the show, Omnivision demonstrated its OX05C1S GS HDR sensor, which uses Nyxel near-infrared technology to achieve high-resolution imaging in near-dark conditions. By shrinking its package by 30%, OmniVision said it allows unobtrusive integration into rearview mirrors or vehicle pillars.
In parallel, Tier-1 supplier Aptiv showcased its Advanced Occupancy Classification software, using a single interior camera to differentiate between adults, infants, children, and inanimate objects.
Aptiv said this camera-only method reached 100% accuracy in Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standard 208 tests, a U.S. regulation, and cut system costs by up to 40% by removing the need for in-seat pressure sensors.
Exterior perception by single-exposure HDR and imaging radar
For outside driver assistance and self-driving features, engineers have to deal with problems such as bright sun glare, dark tunnels, and flickering LED traffic lights.
To address these challenges, Omnivision presented its 3MP TheiaCel image sensor, which offers 140 decibels of single-exposure high dynamic range. Unlike older multi-exposure methods that can cause motion blur at high speeds, the company said this single-exposure approach keeps images clear in bright and dark areas and reduces flicker.
Similarly, SmartSens Technology showed its 8.3MP SC860AT CMOS sensor, which features Lofic HDR 2.0 and is compliant with ISO 26262 ASIL-B and ISO 21434. The sensor was demonstrated with SmartSens subsidiary Flyingchip’s M2 automotive vision-processing SoC, which integrates a neural processing unit and complies with AEC-Q100 Grade 2 automotive standards and ISO 26262 ASIL-B/D functional safety levels.
On the central computing side, Samsung showed its ISOCELL Auto 1H1 and 4AC image sensors alongside a virtual validation partnership with Synopsys and Ansys. Incorporating digital twin models of Samsung sensors into simulation software enables virtual perception validation, shortening product development cycles by up to 12 months, the company said.
Different compute architectures
Discussions about vehicle computing indicated a move away from full centralization toward smarter zonal processing. Automakers used to want all processing in one central computer, but, at AutoSens USA 2026, experts from NXP, Stellantis, and Bosch, pointed out that this causes heat problems and needs too much wiring. Now, the industry is moving to zonal systems, where AI processing happens at the edge, and only key data goes back to the main processor.
Demonstrating this edge-compute trend, STMicroelectronics showcased its STM32N6 microcontroller, featuring an integrated Neural-ART NPU delivering 600 billion operations per second at 3 TOPS per watt. The company showed a demo that included real-time face recognition running directly on the microcontroller.
Meanwhile, high-speed data transfer sparked competition between networking standards. Valens Semiconductor showed its VA7000 chipsets supporting MIPI A-PHY, while Omnivision showcased its 3MP camera sensor featuring an integrated Automotive SerDes Alliance Motion Link serializer.
Cybersecurity and post-quantum cryptography
As software-defined vehicles become increasingly connected, regulatory oversight is expanding beyond standard automotive rules to encompass the European Cyber Resilience Act.
The regulation mandates strict cybersecurity baselines, vulnerability patching, and hardware secure-boot mechanisms for digital products in Europe. Separately, the U.S. National Security Agency’s CNSA 2.0 requirements mandate a transition to post-quantum cryptography to defend against future quantum computing attacks.
At AutoSens Europe, Microchip showed its Trust Shield TS1800 and TS50x Platform root of trust controllers, using an Arm Cortex-M4F processor to run lattice-based post-quantum cryptographic algorithms. The hardware anchors trust directly in physical silicon by monitoring flash memory in real time to prevent firmware tampering.

AI in the Software-Defined Vehicle
Microchip Acquires Edge AI Chip Startup Hailo
Automotive Cybersecurity: AI Attack Surfaces Grow

articles.title: Why Reliable Backup and Off-Grid Power Matters on Farms - Tech Guide
articles.text:
Australian farms don’t run on a nine-to-five schedule, and neither can their power supply. With systems such as irrigation pumps, cold storage, milking sheds and ventilation for animals all relying on a consistent electricity supply, the thought of a blackout, however brief, is potentially devastating.
Many rural properties are either located on a remote site or are on a weak grid connection that can suffer blackouts during severe weather or at periods of high demand.
This is where diesel generators continue to shine as the foundation of rural energy resilience.
Why Reliable Power is Essential for Farm Survival
Unlike in the city, where a short power outage is only a minor inconvenience, for the farmer, it can be a disaster:
- Dairy and livestock producers lose ventilation, cooling, and automated feeding systems, putting animal welfare and yield at risk.
- Cold storage and produce storage facilities can spoil entire batches of stock within hours.
- During peak growing times, irrigation systems miss critical watering windows.
- Remote homesteads lack water pumps, communications, and household power.
Moreover, because many farming operations take place outside the reach of the electric grid, a backup diesel generator for farms is often a matter of survival.
Why Diesel Generators Are a Perfect Fit for Farms
There are many factors that make a diesel generator for farms suitable;
Built for Continuous, Heavy-Duty Use
Whereas small portable units are designed to run intermittently, a generator for use on a farm is built to run for long periods without interruption. Diesel engines are also better at withstanding the high temperatures of continuous useand are generally considered more hardy than their petrol counterparts. Diesel generators provide off grid power and are the preferred choice for heavy machinery which is operated day in and day out.
High Power Outputs for High Demand Equipment
Farms typically require more power to run high-intensity equipment such as pumps, augers, cold rooms, welders, or grain handling machinery. Diesel generators are ideally suited to providing prime power to this sort of equipment.
Fuel Efficiency and Long Run Times
Diesel fuel has a higher energy density than petrol or LPG fuels, meaning a given volume of diesel will produce more energy. This means a diesel generator can either run more equipment for a given amount of fuel, or run for significantly longer on the same amount of fuel. For remote properties without ready access to fuel depots, this can mean the difference between getting a week’s work done, or a month’s work done.
Simpler Designs and Low Maintenance
Compared to other forms of off grid power generation, diesel generators have far fewer components that require specialist servicing. This often means that repairs and servicing can be carried out by the generator owner, which saves money and time.
Reliable Regardless of Weather
While solar panels and battery storage are excellent additions to a farm’s power supply, they have one major weakness: the weather. Diesel generators provide a more consistent output of power regardless of cloudy conditions or seasonal variations. Diesel generators have become the backbone power supply for many farms, while solar and battery systems offer supplementary energy production.
Common Farm Applications for Diesel Generators
Some of the most common uses of diesel generators for farms are as follows:
- Irrigation and water pumping: Keeping crops watered on schedule, even when the grid is down.
- Housing systems for animals: Power for ventilation, heating, lighting, and automated feed systems.
- Cold storage and dairying: Protection of perishable stock and milk from spoilage.
- Machinery sheds and workshops: Running welders, compressors, and power tools in areas without grid access.
- Backup solar/hybrid systems: Step in during a power outage or low-generation season to keep the entire house powered.
Choosing the Right Generator for Your Property
The size of the unit is of particular importance because a small generator will wear out faster under a heavy load, and a large one will unnecessarily waste fuel. To balance things out, it is critical to analyse the current electricity demand in terms of kilowatts, with special attention to surge power (start-up power) required to start pumps and prime movers.
This is why people should entrust this task to experts. Able Power helps farm owners select diesel generators with the power necessary to meet the electricity demand at their agricultural holding. Whether you need a complete turnkey solution or a generator to supplement your solar power system, Able Power will help you achieve value for money.
FAQs
Do I need a diesel generator for my farm?
A diesel generator is a great backup power source if you have solar power installed on your property. Solar and battery storage systems are weather-dependent, but diesel generators can provide consistent power regardless of conditions.
How long will a diesel generator last?
With the right maintenance, diesel generators can run for prolonged periods of time, even weeks at a time.
What size generator do I need for my farm?
This depends on the equipment you need to run, and recommendations should be made according to the load requirements. It is not recommended to base a generator size for a property on square meters.
Final Word
Off-grid and remote farms cannot afford to have their electricity supply interrupted. Diesel generators are the preferred method of delivering electricity to farms because they are cost-effective, reliable, and able to run-in all-weather conditions.
They provide a vital backup power source that allows farms to keep irrigation, livestock, cold storage, and other essential equipment running. To protect your farm’s electrical supply, contact Able Power to discuss your backup power needs with an experienced technician.

articles.title: Amazon lance ses nouveaux Kindle et fait grimper les prix
articles.text:
Les nouvelles liseuses Kindle sont officiellement là. Amazon vient de dévoiler sa nouvelle gamme, entièrement repensée, avec un Kindle standard, un Kindle Papierwhite et un Kindle Colorsoft arborant un nouveau profil. Plus fins, plus légers, ils profitent désormais d’un écran bord à bord sans bordure surélevée et une mauvaise surprise : un tarif qui grimpe sensiblement par rapport à la précédente génération de Kindle.
Un Kindle 6 pouces cher payé
Pour son nouveau modèle standard, Amazon a opté pour une configuration plus compacte. Le nouveau Kindle 6 pouces intègre 16 Go de stockage et offre jusqu’à 6 semaines d’autonomie d’après Amazon et serait jusqu’à 30% plus rapide pour ouvrir les ouvrages. Le boîtier utilise des matériaux recyclés tout comme la batterie qui intègre du cobalt entièrement recyclé.
L’utilisation de ces matériaux recyclés n’a toutefois aucun impact positif sur le tarif de vente. Bien au contraire. Car le ticket d’entrée pour le nouveau Kindle de base s’affiche 154,99 euros, contre 109,99 euros pour le précédent modèle sorti en 2024, soit une augmentation de 45 euros.
Amazon a par ailleurs décliné ce modèle d’entrée de gamme dans une version avec un dos en aluminium arborant une finition mate et équipé de 32 Go de stockage. Cette déclinaison, disponible dans deux nouveaux coloris (Bleu Alpin Aluminium et Vert d’eau Aluminium), est quant à elle proposée à 194,99 euros.
Les Kindle Paperwhite et Colorsoft s’affinent sauf sur les prix
Du côté du Kindle Paperwhite, Amazon a imaginé sa nouvelle génération plus fine et plus légère. La liseuse, dotée de 16 Go de stockage, est toujours dotée de son écran de 7 pouces conserve sa résistance à l’eau et promet une autonomie pouvant aller jusqu’à 12 semaines.
Le Kindle Colorsoft quant à lui conserve son écran couleur de 7 pouces et ses 16 Go de stockage, mais Amazon y a intégré une nouvelle technologie pour garantir la clarté et un contraste élevé.
Le Kindle Paperwhite est proposé à 209,99 euros contre 169,99 euros pour la précédente génération. Ce modèle est décliné dans une version Signature (en couleurs Graphite et Vert d’eau) affichée à 259,99 euros embarquant 32 Go, un dos en aluminium et un éclairage à ajustement automatique, une recharge sans fil par station d’accueil et la possibilité de tourner les pages à l’aide d’un double tapotement.
Le Kindle Colorsoft est vendu 299,99 euros dans sa version de base (contre 269,99 euros pour la précédente génération), et 329,99 euros pour sa version Signature dotée d’un boîtier en aluminium (coloris Graphite et Figue), l’éclairage auto-ajustable, la recharge par station d’accueil et, là encore, la possibilité de tourner les pages avec un double tapotement.

articles.title: À 16 ans, il est soupçonné d’avoir dirigé un groupe de ransomware responsable de 1 000 attaques
articles.text:
Le principal opérateur présumé de KillSec n’a que 16 ans. Mercredi, la police espagnole l’a interpellé dans la province d’Alicante, au cours d’une opération coordonnée à l’échelle européenne. Ce groupe de ransomware est soupçonné de près de 1 000 attaques dans le monde depuis 2024.
Les enquêteurs ont identifié quatre rôles au sein de KillSec, et l’adolescent occupait celui d’administrateur principal. Lors de cette journée d’action, les forces de l’ordre ont aussi arrêté deux hommes d’une vingtaine d’années, au Royaume-Uni et en Roumanie. Les enquêteurs tombent régulièrement sur des pirates très jeunes, en France aussi, où un hacker de 18 ans a été placé en détention provisoire début septembre dans l'affaire du piratage des impôts, tandis qu’un complice présumé de 16 ans a été entendu. Derrière KillSec, les polices européennes et le FBI ont trouvé un service de ransomware loué à d’autres pirates, avec un adolescent à sa tête.
Arrestations et saisies dans quatre pays européens
En 2025, le bureau du FBI de San Juan, à Porto Rico, a demandé à la Guardia Civil de l’aider à retrouver des membres de KillSec installés en Espagne. Les gendarmes espagnols ont localisé le suspect dans la province d’Alicante grâce à une simple photo de profil. En Catalogne, la police régionale a ouvert de son côté une enquête après une attaque contre une organisation de la région, début 2025. Ses enquêteurs estiment les dégâts à près d’un million d’euros et soupçonnent KillSec d’en être l’auteur.
Europol et Eurojust ont ensuite coordonné le travail des polices de plusieurs pays, avec l’appui des spécialistes en cybersécurité de Bitdefender et de Group-IB. Pour Eurojust, les autorités ont « démantelé avec succès un groupe de ransomware ». Lors des perquisitions dans la province d’Alicante, les gendarmes ont saisi du matériel informatique et des portefeuilles de cryptomonnaies. Dès une première analyse, ils ont repéré des transactions qui correspondent aux rançons versées par certaines victimes.
La police et le parquet de Hambourg ont piloté l'opération KillSwitch. Leurs enquêteurs ont mis hors ligne cinq serveurs, dont le serveur principal du groupe et plusieurs machines de stockage des données volées, puis placé sous scellés 110 téraoctets de données. Une bannière de saisie est désormais affichée sur cinq noms de domaine de KillSec.
La justice de Porto Rico a demandé l'extradition du suspect arrêté au Royaume-Uni, a précisé un porte-parole d’Europol à Reuters. En Roumanie, les procureurs spécialisés dans la criminalité organisée ont interpellé un homme de 24 ans et perquisitionné quatre logements à Bucarest et dans le comté de Vaslui. Le 1er octobre, ils ont demandé à un tribunal de Bucarest son placement en détention provisoire pour 30 jours. Il est présumé innocent. Le développeur présumé du groupe, qui a eu 18 ans en août, était mineur au moment d’une partie des faits. Les enquêteurs l’ont identifié sans l’arrêter.
Les méthodes de KillSec pour extorquer ses victimes
En juin 2024, KillSec a ouvert son ransomware à des affiliés, d’après les chercheurs de Rapid7. Des pirates extérieurs pouvaient alors louer les outils du groupe et lancer eux-mêmes des attaques. Pour entrer dans les systèmes des organisations, les membres de KillSec exploitaient des failles logicielles et des accès mal sécurisés, en particulier ceux du stockage cloud, d'après la police de Hambourg. Ils copiaient ensuite les données internes sensibles vers leurs serveurs, puis affichaient le nom de chaque victime sur leur site de fuite du dark web. Faute de paiement, les fichiers volés pouvaient être proposés en téléchargement libre.
Les procureurs roumains ajoutent que les membres du groupe achetaient des identifiants d’accès sur le dark web. Ils envoyaient aussi à leurs cibles un extrait des données volées en guise de preuve, et menaçaient de les revendre à d’autres groupes criminels si la victime ne payait pas.
Au total, les enquêteurs examinent près de 1 000 attaques présumées, dont environ 500 réussies. La police espagnole compte plus de 280 victimes, et la police de Hambourg au moins 70 attaques en Allemagne, dont 18 liées à la ville. Le groupe « a obtenu d’importantes rançons », a indiqué Europol, cité par Reuters.
Les policiers allemands ont aussi découvert que KillSec utilisait l’intelligence artificielle pour bâtir son infrastructure et repérer ses victimes potentielles, sans donner plus de détails. Dans son rapport 2026 sur la cybercriminalité, Europol mettait en garde contre l'essor d’outils d’IA capables de mener seuls des opérations criminelles complètes.
Les enquêteurs analysent maintenant les appareils saisis et remontent la piste des cryptomonnaies du groupe, avec l’espoir d’identifier d'autres victimes et d'autres suspects. Pour la police de Hambourg, les trois arrestations sont provisoires, et ses enquêteurs continuent de rechercher d'autres membres de KillSec.

articles.title: Add secure Web Search to Claude Desktop with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore | Amazon Web Services
articles.text:
Artificial Intelligence
Add secure Web Search to Claude Desktop with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
Claude Desktop on Amazon Bedrock provides powerful AI assistance, but without integrated web search, responses are limited to the model’s training knowledge cutoff. When you need current information, such as recent documentation updates, live pricing, or weather updates, the model can’t retrieve it on its own.
Amazon Bedrock AgentCore is a platform to build, connect, and optimize agents at scale, with any framework or model. With AgentCore Gateway, a capability of Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, you can close this knowledge cutoff gap by connecting Claude Desktop to Web Search. Web Search is a fully managed, Model Context Protocol (MCP)-compatible web search capability backed by an Amazon web index that spans tens of billions of documents. All query traffic stays within AWS infrastructure, with no external API keys to manage and no queries leaving your boundary.
With Claude Desktop, you can use managed MCP servers to connect to an AgentCore Gateway with the Web Search target enabled. In this post, we walk through the steps to set up this integration and use JSON Web Token (JWT)-based inbound authentication to secure the communication.
Architecture
Many enterprises running on AWS use AWS IAM Identity Center for single sign-on (SSO) access to their AWS accounts. In this walkthrough, we use AWS IAM Identity Center as the authentication source for the AgentCore Gateway. With this setup, Claude Desktop on Amazon Bedrock can invoke Web Search through a trusted, enterprise-managed identity flow. This approach aligns with existing organizational identity governance. No separate credentials or third-party identity providers are required.
To bridge AWS IAM Identity Center with the AgentCore Gateway JWT-based authentication, we use Amazon Cognito as a federation layer with the OAuth 2.0 authorization code grant flow. IAM Identity Center handles user authentication through Security Assertion Markup Language (SAML). Amazon Cognito issues JWTs, and the AgentCore Gateway validates them on each request. The entire authentication chain stays within AWS.
The following sequence diagram illustrates this authentication flow.
Prerequisites
To follow along with the steps in this post, you need the following:
- An AWS account with permissions to create AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) roles and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore resources.
- Admin access to your management account in AWS Organizations (for AWS IAM Identity Center configuration).
- AWS IAM Identity Center preconfigured for SSO access to AWS accounts.
- Claude Desktop set up with Amazon Bedrock as the inference provider.
- The AWS Command Line Interface (AWS CLI) v2 installed and configured.
- Python 3.10 or later.
- The Boto3 SDK updated to the latest version.
Web Search on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore is currently available in the US East (N. Virginia) AWS Region (us-east-1), Europe (Ireland) Region (eu-west-1), and Asia Pacific (Tokyo) Region (ap-northeast-1). Verify that your gateway is created in one of these Regions.
Configuration
The configuration involves setting up the authentication chain (AWS IAM Identity Center to Amazon Cognito to JWT) and then wiring the AgentCore Gateway into Claude Desktop. We walk through each step in the following section.
Step 1: Create an Amazon Cognito user pool
In your target AWS account, create an Amazon Cognito user pool that will serve as the OpenID Connect (OIDC) token issuer for the AgentCore Gateway.
Save these values for later steps:
- User Pool ID: $USER_POOL_ID.
- Domain: <your-unique-prefix>.auth.<region>.amazoncognito.com.
- Audience: urn:amazon:cognito:sp:<user-pool-id>.
- ACS URL: https://<your-unique-prefix>.auth.<region>.amazoncognito.com/saml2/idpresponse.
Step 2: Configure IAM Identity Center SAML application
In your AWS Organizations management account, create a SAML application that federates with Cognito:
- Open IAM Identity Center console.
- Choose Applications, Add application, I have an application I want to set up, SAML 2.0, and then Next.
- Fill in the following details: 
         
  - Display name: AgentCore Web Search.
  - Select Manually type your metadata value. 
           
    - ACS URL: https://<your-unique-prefix>.auth.<region>.amazoncognito.com/saml2/idpresponse.
    - Audience: urn:amazon:cognito:sp:<user-pool-id>.
  - Download the SAML metadata XML file and choose Submit.
  - After the application is created, edit the attribute mappings and insert the following values: 
           
    - Subject, ${user:subject}, Format: Persistent.
    - Email, ${user:email}, Format: Basic.
  - Assign the users or groups that would have access to Web Search.
Step 3: Wire SAML IdP into Cognito
Back in the target account, register IAM Identity Center as a SAML identity provider in your Cognito user pool:
Step 4: Create Cognito app client for Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
Create an app client with a client secret. Claude Desktop uses this client to initiate the OAuth flow, which authenticates the user through IAM Identity Center and obtains a JWT for the AgentCore Gateway:
Note the Client ID and Client Secret from the output. These are your application client ID and secret.
Step 5: Configure AgentCore Gateway with Web Search tool
In this step, we create a new AgentCore Gateway with Inbound Auth Type as JSON Web Tokens (JWT). For this configuration, we use the Cognito user pool ID and application client ID that were created in the prior steps.
Run the following Python script to create the gateway with the required configurations, replacing all placeholders with actual values from your environment.
You now have an AgentCore Gateway with Web Search tool, with JWT-based inbound authorization.
Step 6: Configure Claude Desktop
Use the steps in the Claude Desktop configuration documentation to access the configuration window for Claude Desktop with Amazon Bedrock. After you open it, choose Connectors and Extensions, then choose Add server, and then choose Blank.
The following screenshot shows the configuration window with these options.
Enter the following details:
- Name: websearchtool.
- Transport: Streamable HTTP.
- URL: Enter the gateway resource URL for the AgentCore Gateway created in Step 5.
- OAuth: Bring your own client.
- Client ID: Enter the client ID for the app client created in Step 4.
- Client Secret: Enter the client secret for the app client created in Step 4.
- Authorization Server: Enter ["https://<your-unique-prefix>.auth.<region>.amazoncognito.com/oauth2/authorize"].
- Scope: openid.
- Callback host: localhost.
- Callback port: 53280.
When you’re done, choose sign in and test. This should open a browser for you to authenticate, redirecting you to your AWS IAM Identity Center SSO login. Enter your credentials to authenticate. If successful, you should see a message such as, “Authorization complete. You can close this tab and return to Claude.”
Back in Claude Desktop, you should see a successful MCP registration message like in the following image.
Claude Desktop will now discover the WebSearchTool through the MCP tools/list call. It invokes the tool automatically whenever the model needs current information from the web.
Testing and validation
In your preferred interface (for example, Chat or Cowork), send a query that requires Claude Desktop to retrieve the latest results. You should see a tool execution approval box, indicating that Claude has successfully discovered the Web Search tool. On approval, you should see the web search results included in the response.
The dialog shows the query Claude wants to run and offers three options: Deny, Allow for this task, or Allow once. On approval, Web Search results are included in the response.
Clean up
If you created resources while following along, perform the following steps to delete them:
Finally, in the IAM Identity Center console in the management account, delete the SAML application you created in Step 2.
Conclusion
In this post, we walked through integrating Web Search on AgentCore with Claude Desktop. While this walkthrough uses AWS IAM Identity Center as the identity provider, the same pattern works with any SAML or OIDC-compatible identity provider. You can substitute your existing IdP by configuring it as a federation source in Amazon Cognito. This approach closes the web search gap without introducing third-party dependencies, and all queries stay within your AWS boundary.
To get started, follow the steps above to set up the integration in your own environment. For advanced gateway configurations, see the AgentCore Gateway Developer Guide. To learn more about Web Search, see the Web Search documentation.

articles.title: Bradley Cooper s'empare de G.I. Joe avec un reboot complet et la fin du cross-over Transformers
articles.text:
Paramount n’abandonne pas G.I. Joe malgré les échecs à répétition. Après celui de Snake Eyes en 2021 (40 millions de dollars de recettes dans le monde, pour un budget d’au moins 88 millions), le studio tente un nouveau coup de poker.
La saga G.I. Joe repart à zéro. Pour incarner le légendaire Duke, le chef de terrain autrefois joué par Channing Tatum dans les films de 2009 et 2013, Paramount a choisi Bradley Cooper.
Douze fois nommé aux Oscars, Bradley Cooper enfile le treillis pour G.I. Joe
Qu’est-ce qui pousse l’un des acteurs-réalisateurs les plus cotés d’Hollywood (A Star Is Born, Maestro) à enfiler l’uniforme d’un soldat en plastique ? Cooper n’a pourtant pas de temps libre. Il écrit, réalise et tourne actuellement le préquel d’Ocean’s Eleven, aux côtés de Margot Robbie et Monica Barbaro.
En confiant le rôle de Duke (Conrad Hauser de son vrai nom) à un acteur estampillé « prestige », Paramount montre son ambition : transformer une licence de jouets autrefois décriée pour sa beaufitude en blockbuster d’action haut de gamme. Les deux premiers films, avec Channing Tatum, avaient pourtant rapporté près de 680 millions de dollars dans le monde avant que la machine ne s’enraye.
Danny McBride aux commandes : la promesse d’un ton corrosif
Paramount a confié la réalisation à Danny McBride, un choix connu depuis la mi-juillet. Il est une figure culte de la comédie américaine abrasive (The Righteous Gemstones, Vice Principals).
Coécrit avec ses compères habituels Jeff Fradley et John Carcieri, ce nouveau G.I. Joe pourrait bien éviter le piège du film d’action sans âme. McBride apporte dans ses bagages un humour grinçant et un sens de la déconstruction des figures viriles qui pourraient faire un bien fou à une franchise historiquement trop premier degré.
Le crossover avec Transformers passe à la trappe
Paramount fait aussi machine arrière. À la fin de Transformers: Rise of the Beasts, en 2023, une scène post-générique annonçait une alliance entre les Autobots et l’organisation G.I. Joe, et le studio avait officialisé ce film commun en 2024.
Paramount a confirmé que ce crossover, une tentative de copier l’univers connecté de Marvel, n’est plus en développement. Le nouveau G.I. Joe est « découplé » de Transformers, ce qui laisse à McBride et Cooper le champ libre, loin du bazar cosmique des robots géants.
Paramount n’a donné ni date de sortie, ni le reste de la distribution, ni l’intrigue détaillée. Cet été, Danny McBride espérait tourner « l’an prochain ». D’ici là, Bradley Cooper est encore sur le tournage du préquel d’Ocean’s Eleven.

articles.title: Amazon fait déjà passer le nouveau Google Pixel 11, avec son téléobjectif x5, sous les 750 € — Frandroid
articles.text:
Le Pixel 11 est le plus accessible des nouveaux smartphones Google, sous les Pixel 11 Pro, Pixel 11 Pro XL et Pixel 11 Pro Fold. Ce qu’il faut retenir, c’est qu’il garde le téléobjectif x5 apparu sur le Pixel 10 et ajoute une grosse dose d’IA avec Android 17. Noté 8/10 dans notre test, il visait à son lancement des concurrents vendus autour de 1 000 euros. Bon, à ce tarif, c’était discutable. Mais avec l’offre du jour, il passe à moins de 750 euros, et ça change forcément la donne.
Les atouts du Google Pixel 11
- Un téléobjectif x5 qui reste efficace jusqu’au zoom x30
- La transcription et la traduction des messages vocaux par l’IA
- Sept années de mises à jour promises par Google
Lancé à 999 euros, le Pixel 11 (coloris Pistache, 256 Go) s’affiche à 848,88 euros sur Amazon. L’offre de remboursement de 100 euros ramène ensuite la facture à 748,88 euros, soit environ 250 euros d’économie par rapport au lancement.
Si, par la suite, l’offre mentionnée dans cet article n’est plus disponible, merci de jeter un coup d’œil ci-dessous afin de dénicher d’autres offres concernant le Google Pixel 11. Le tableau s’actualise automatiquement.
Un zoom qui fait le travail
Le téléobjectif x5 hérité du Pixel 10 reste l’argument numéro un de ce modèle. Dans notre test, on l’a jugé efficace jusqu’au zoom x30. C’est rare sur un smartphone qui n’est pas estampillé Pro. Le capteur grand-angle, annoncé comme plus efficace par Google, livre de très bonnes photos, et les selfies suivent. Le bloc optique change de design, sans renier l’allure originale qui fait l’identité visuelle des Pixel depuis plusieurs générations.
La Capture magique et le mode vidéo Créateur complètent le tableau, avec la patte logicielle qui fait la réputation de Google. Bon, tout n’est pas parfait. La fonction HiLight manque à l’appel, et la dalle OLED fait l’impasse sur la technologie LTPO (celle qui ajuste finement le taux de rafraîchissement pour ménager la batterie). Sa haute luminosité rattrape en partie le coup, notamment pour la lisibilité en extérieur.
Beaucoup d’IA, un peu moins de muscle
Le Pixel 11 tourne sous Android 17, avec une interface qui fait toujours la part belle à l’IA. La fonction la plus utile au quotidien ? La transcription et la traduction automatiques des messages vocaux. Pratique quand on ne peut pas écouter un audio de deux minutes dans le métro. Google promet aussi sept ans de mises à jour, de quoi garder ce téléphone longtemps sans craindre d’être lâché en route.
Le nouveau processeur Tensor G6 a en revanche ses limites. Les Pixel 11 ont du mal avec certains jeux, et la puce ne serait pas la seule en cause. Ajoutez des charges filaire et sans fil peu rapides, malgré les progrès annoncés sur le sans-fil, et l’absence de compatibilité Wi-Fi 7. Bref, les joueurs exigeants regarderont ailleurs. Pour la photo et les outils d’IA, il fait carrément le taf.
Pour le détail de chaque critère, de la photo aux performances, rendez-vous sur notre test du Google Pixel 11, signé Xavier Regord.
Si vous hésitez avec un Pixel 11 Pro ou un modèle plus ancien, notre guide des meilleurs smartphones Google Pixel vous aidera à faire le tri.

articles.title: Sweden’s Omnio raises €2.9 million to advance its plasminogen-based therapy for hard-to-heal chronic wounds | EU-Startups
articles.text:
Omnio, a Umeå-based BioTech startup, has raised an oversubscribed €2.9 million round from existing investors and shareholders to advance its plasminogen-based therapy for hard-to-heal chronic wounds toward clinical studies.
This funding follows a €4.3 million financing round completed in spring 2025 to complete its GMP manufacturing process and move toward clinical trials. The company notes that the development has progressed according to plan since this round.
“This financing demonstrates our continuous progress and strong confidence from our current investors. Their support allows us to continue the development and puts us in a stronger position ahead of our next financing round for clinical studies,” said Felipe Velasquez, CEO of Omnio.
Founded on research by Professor Tor Ny at Umeå University (also head of R&D at Omnio), Omnio is developing plasminogen-based therapies for chronic wounds and related conditions. The company states that it is advancing a biologic treatment designed to address the underlying biology of impaired wound healing.
Its lead indication is diabetic foot ulcers (DFU), a condition in which wounds can be difficult to heal, with limited effective treatment options. According to the company, more than half a billion people worldwide live with diabetes, and up to one-third will develop a foot ulcer during their lifetime.
“These wounds can become chronic and devastating — severely impacting mobility, quality of life and productivity, while putting patients at risk of amputation. For healthcare systems, the burden is equally significant, with advanced-stage diabetic foot ulcers costing an estimated €50,000 per wound episode,” the company mentioned in the press release.
At the core of Omnio’s therapy is plasminogen, which is a natural protein with pro-inflammatory and immunoregulatory properties that helps the body clear damaged tissue, fight infection, and regenerate skin. In people with chronic wounds, that healing process stalls. Omnio claims to restart it.
Its mission is to help people with hard-to-heal diabetic foot ulcers regain mobility and avoid amputation. Its lead drug candidate is a recombinant form of plasminogen.
The Swedish startup notes that it has established its master cell bank and is now scaling up manufacturing in preparation for a GMP batch that will be used in toxicology studies. These studies are required before submitting applications to begin clinical trials. The clinical study programme will begin with a Phase I/IIa safety and early-efficacy study in patients with diabetic foot ulcers.
“Our ambition is to move into patient studies during 2027. We are already evaluating CROs, investigators and trial countries across Europe to support the launch of the clinical programme,” added Velasquez.
While diabetic foot ulcers remain the company’s primary focus, it sees potential applications for its plasminogen platform across a broader range of chronic wound conditions, including venous leg ulcers (VLU), burns, tympanic membrane perforations, infection, and periodontitis.
Omnio plans to open its next financing round in Q1 2027 to fund clinical development through first efficacy data. “We are structuring the next financing round around key development milestones as we prepare to enter clinical studies,” said Velasquez.
“The wound healing market is mostly a medical devices market, but nothing has really moved the needle in hard-to-heal wounds. We are not developing another medical device. We are developing a biologic therapy that addresses the biology of wound healing and the root cause of why these wounds stay open,” he stated.

articles.title: AI Agents Aimed SQL Injection at US and Canadian Government Sites
articles.text:
AI agents appear to have attempted to hack a US Department of Education website and a Library and Archives Canada service while trying to access public data, according to AI research lab Transluce.
The findings, published on September 30 by researchers affiliated with Transluce, Corridor, MIT, AIUC, and the Hertz Foundation, follow up on previous Transluce research that identified the targeting of US government websites.
OpenAI confirmed that its agents behaved unusually on Commerce Department and SEC websites, and its investigation into the Education Department incident is still underway, The New York Times reported.
Transluce researchers found nothing in the data they analyzed to suggest the agents obtained non-public information.
The Education Department incident took place in June, when agents apparently searching for school statistics sent over 200,000 requests to the department’s Civil Rights Data Collection website. Among them was a basic SQL injection probe.
“Data stored on this website appears to match a web search task in Google’s DeepSearchQA benchmark, suggesting that the agents were not given a hacking-related task but were being graded on their ability to successfully retrieve specific niche information from the internet,” Transluce notes.
The researchers also observed more than 10,000 requests that included a tag beginning with “oai”, which could indicate the involvement of OpenAI agents. The Department of Education, notified on September 25, said it observed no impact on its services.
Separately, Portugal’s Arquivo.pt web archive captured 899 requests to Library and Archives Canada’s collection search service in May and July. The requests were associated with retrieving data on Canadian divorce records from 1905 to 1911.
Of these, 13 contained attack payloads: three SQL injection probes, a cross-site scripting probe, and requests that tested input handling, output formats, and a debug flag.
“We do not believe that these probes were successful: each one came back as a normal HTTP 200 with an empty record page, with nothing to indicate the database acted on the input or that any extra data was returned,” Transluce says.
While Transluce does not confidently blame OpenAI for the Canadian attempts, it says the tactics match those of agent activity previously linked to the company.
In a September 29 statement, Canada’s Communications Security Establishment said there is “no indication that government systems have been compromised at this time.” It noted that public-facing government websites routinely receive automated and potentially malicious requests, and that the Canadian Centre for Cyber Security is assessing the reports.
OpenAI told Reuters it was “aware of reports of OpenAI models attempting to access publicly available information” from Canadian government websites. A spokesperson said the company was reviewing the findings and had given Canadian officials an initial briefing.
Transluce also observed automated workflows, which it attributes to AI agents with varying levels of confidence, that used aggressive tactics short of hacking against websites of the White House, the Departments of War, Justice, and Commerce, the CDC and SEC, and state agencies in California, Maryland, Illinois, Texas, and New York.
The techniques included making accounts with disposable email addresses, bypassing anti-bot controls, reusing exposed credentials, and flooding sites with requests.
Part of this activity overlaps with traffic confirmed as linked to OpenAI, and some agents explicitly labeled themselves as associated with the company. Still, Transluce does not blame OpenAI for the activity overall.

articles.title: Dell asks admins to patch max severity CSM flaws as soon as possible
articles.text:
Dell has patched two maximum severity vulnerabilities in the Container Storage Modules (CSM) that connect Dell enterprise storage arrays to Kubernetes environments.
CSM supports Dell's primary storage platforms (PowerStore, PowerScale, PowerFlex, PowerMax, and Unity XT), and it extends the capabilities of the standard Container Storage Interface (CSI) drivers for Kubernetes.
In a security advisory published on Thursday, Dell said that both critical security flaws were found in the Dell CSM Authorization security module and stem from "missing authentication for critical functions" weaknesses.
The first (tracked as CVE-2026-63688) allows unauthenticated remote attackers to access storage backend administrator credentials for all registered storage arrays and bypass authorization to gain full administrative control over the storage infrastructure.
Successful exploitation of the second flaw (CVE-2026-63692), present in the authorization proxy and tenant service, also allows threat actors to gain admin privileges by bypassing authentication controls.
"This vulnerability is considered critical as it enables an unauthenticated attacker to gain complete administrative control over the authorization service, potentially allowing unauthorized access to and manipulation of storage resources across all tenants," Dell warned.
The same day, the company also patched four additional critical-severity Dell CSM security issues that remote attackers can also exploit without privileges to gain root on cluster nodes (CVE-2026-67269), gain administrative access to the CSM Authorization proxy (CVE-2026-54472), forge authentication tokens to gain administrative privileges (CVE-2026-61421), and bypass Kubernetes access controls for cluster-wide read access to Kubernetes Secrets (CVE-2026-67273).
"Dell recommends customers to upgrade at the earliest opportunity," the company added, advising customers to update their container storage modules to version 1.18.0 or later, which patches these flaws.
Dell vulnerabilities exploited in the wild
While Dell has yet to flag these security issues as actively exploited, state-sponsored hackers have abused other Dell vulnerabilities in attacks in recent years.
For instance, the North Korean Lazarus hacking group deployed a Windows rootkit on victims' systems by exploiting an insufficient access control vulnerability (CVE-2021-21551) in the Dell dbutil driver.
More recently, in February, Mandiant and the Google Threat Intelligence Group (GTIG) revealed that a suspected Chinese state-backed hacking group (UNC6201) had been exploiting a maximum-severity hardcoded-credential vulnerability (CVE-2026-22769) in Dell RecoverPoint for Virtual Machines since at least mid-2024 to deploy malware payloads and create hidden network interfaces on VMware ESXi servers.
The security researchers also found overlaps between UNC6201 and the Silk Typhoon Chinese cyberespionage group, known for targeting government agencies with custom Spawnant and Zipline malware in Ivanti zero-day attacks.
Days later, the U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) ordered government agencies to patch vulnerable Dell systems on their networks within three days.

articles.title: De las dos opciones que TSMC maneja para abrir su nuevo campus una cosa llama la atención: ninguna está en Europa
articles.text:
El complejo de fábricas que está construyendo TSMC en Arizona (EEUU) es titánico. Su primera planta de producción de semiconductores de este campus inició la operación hace dos años, aunque no alcanzó la fabricación a gran escala en el nodo N4 (4 nm) hasta el año pasado. No obstante, este es solo el primer eslabón de la cadena. La segunda planta estará operativa en 2028 y fabricará circuitos integrados en los nodos N3 (3 nm) y N2 (2 nm).
Y, por último, la tercera fábrica no estará lista del todo hasta finales de esta década y producirá chips en el nodo N2 (2 nm) o, incluso, en un nodo todavía más avanzado. Estas instalaciones son cruciales para que EEUU reduzca su dependencia de los chips que proceden de Asia, por lo que es razonable prever que los problemas que están lastrando la construcción de estas fábricas se terminarán subsanando.
Este proyecto no solo es importante para EEUU; también es crucial para TSMC. Su campus de Phoenix permitirá a medio plazo a esta compañía responder con más eficacia a la enorme demanda de circuitos integrados para aplicaciones de inteligencia artificial (IA). Y, además, reforzar su infraestructura fuera de Taiwán es una medida de cautela frente a un posible conflicto futuro con China. Este escenario, de hecho, ha propiciado que TSMC esté sopesando la posibilidad de construir un segundo gran polo de fabricación de chips en EEUU.
UN VISTAZO A...
Texas es un candidato idóneo
El estado de Texas tiene un ecosistema de fabricación de semiconductores maduro. Samsung y Texas Instruments tienen fábricas de chips muy importantes en Austin, Taylor, Dallas, Richardson y Sherman. Además, el proyecto Terafab de Elon Musk residirá probablemente en Austin y proyecta la construcción de dos grandes líneas de fabricación de chips. Una abastecerá a Tesla, y la otra a SpaceX. Las plantas de Samsung, Texas Instruments y otras compañías más pequeñas han propiciado, además, que la cadena de suministro sea muy robusta.
Estos ingredientes son muy atractivos para TSMC. Tanto, de hecho, que según Bloomberg y DigiTimes está planeando construir en Texas un campus tan ambicioso como el que está desplegando actualmente en Arizona. Por el momento este proyecto está tomando forma y no hay nada confirmado oficialmente, pero estos medios han anticipado que probablemente incluirá varias fábricas de circuitos integrados y requerirá decenas de miles de millones de dólares de inversión. Cada fábrica podría costar al menos 20.000 millones de dólares, que es lo que suele exigir una planta de vanguardia.
Cada fábrica podría costar al menos 20.000 millones de dólares, que es lo que suele exigir una planta de vanguardia
Que este proyecto salga adelante no depende solo de TSMC. En gran medida está en las manos del Gobierno de EEUU porque sin incentivos fiscales jugosos difícilmente se llevará a cabo. Esta compañía taiwanesa asume una parte importante del coste que conlleva la puesta en marcha de sus nuevas plantas, pero no todo. De hecho, el crédito fiscal del 35% aprobado en 2025 por el Congreso es uno de los principales mecanismos con los que EEUU está intentando atraer a su territorio la fabricación de chips avanzados.
Sea como sea, esta moneda tiene otra cara: Europa. La fábrica de chips que TSMC está construyendo en Dresde (Alemania) costará algo más de 10.000 millones de euros, más o menos la mitad que una sola de las plantas de Arizona. Además, esta instalación no pertenece solo a TSMC; estará gestionada por una empresa conjunta en la que también participan Bosch, Infineon y NXP Semiconductors, que cuentan con una participación del 10% cada una, mientras que TSMC controla el 70% restante.
No obstante, por el momento no hay ningún indicio que nos invite a prever que esta última compañía planea expandir más su infraestructura europea.

articles.title: On a testé le Kioxia Exceria Plus G4, le premier SSD PCIe Gen 5 de la marque mise sur la sécurité et le prix
articles.text:
| Capacité de stockage | 1 To, 2 To | 
| Format | M.2 | 
| Norme | PCIe 5.0 | 
| Type de mémoire SSD | TLC | 
| Vitesse lecture | 10000 Mo/s | 
| Durée de vie (TBW) | 1200 To | 
| Dissipateur thermique | Non | 
| Compatible PS5 | Non | 
Le Kioxia Exceria Plus G4 est un module de stockage SSD interne disponible en versions 1 To et 2 To. Il s'agit du premier SSD de la marque japonaise destiné au grand public compatible avec l'interface PCIe Gen 5, le tout assorti d’une promesse de débits séquentiels plus importants que la précédente génération.
À côté des gros joueurs Samsung, SanDisk et, fut un temps, Crucial, une marque poursuit son petit bonhomme de chemin dans la discrétion la plus totale. Le japonais Kioxia continue ainsi de commercialiser des modules de stockage interne et externe pour le marché consumer dans son pays d'origine, mais aussi en Europe, tout en ignorant les États-Unis où il demeure un simple fournisseur OEM pour les constructeurs informatiques.
Cela faisait un peu plus d'un an que Kioxia n'avait pas eu droit à une nouvelle référence dans notre comparatif, et c'est par son module Exceria Plus G4 qu'elle fait son retour en ce début d'automne 2026.
Le Kioxia Exceria Plus G4 a la particularité d'être le premier module interne consumer de la marque à être compatible avec l'interface PCIe Gen 5, ce qui devrait lui permettre de dépasser aisément les vitesses proposées par son prédécesseur Exceria Plus G3, déjà testé dans nos colonnes. Ce n'est pas pour autant le SSD interne le plus véloce du portfolio de la marque, puisque le modèle Pro G4 affiche des débits supérieurs. Néanmoins, l'Exceria Plus G4 est celui qui profite du “meilleur” placement tarifaire… en toute relativité quand on considère l'état désastreux du marché des SSD depuis un an.
Il faut ainsi compter aux alentours de 160 € pour la version 1 To de stockage et 240 € pour la version 2 To (c'est cette dernière qui passe sur notre banc de test). À ce prix-là, Kioxia affiche une fiche technique tout à fait ordinaire pour un module moderne : contrôleur Phison E31T et puce NAND flash à 218 couches 3D TLC, soit mieux que le récent Samsung 990, choix budget de la marque sud-coréenne qui se contentait de mémoire QLC. Du reste, l'endurance certifiée à 1200 TBW et les cinq ans de garantie sont dans les clous.
Tous les miracles sont donc possibles, même celui de voir un SSD PCIe Gen 5 qui n'atteint pas 100 °C lors d'une pleine charge. C'est ainsi que nous a surpris l'Exceria Plus G4 qui, en boucle intense sur CDM, n'a pas dépassé les 81 °C sur la sonde interne, même si nous déconseillons d'approcher un doigt trop près du module. Comme toujours, les benchmarks sont réalisés avec le dissipateur thermique de notre carte mère Asus ROG Crosshair X670E afin de préserver l'intégrité des valeurs par rapport au reste de notre comparatif.
Notre protocole pour évaluer la taille du cache pSLC (le mode le plus véloce lors des gros transferts sur les SSD QLC et TLC) consiste à écrire un flux séquentiel de blocs de 1 Mo sur l'intégralité du disque via AIDA64. Ainsi, nous déterminons à partir de quel point les performances atteignent leur plafond. Ce genre d'opération est rarissime au quotidien, tout du moins pour la grande majorité des utilisateurs, même lors de l'installation d'un jeu lourd dont les fichiers dépassent rarement quelques dizaines de gigaoctets. Ce benchmark est donc illustratif et non pris en compte dans notre appréciation finale.
Le Kioxia Exceria Plus G4 affiche une belle tenue de performance sur notre test avec un débit d'écriture moyen de 3715 Mo/s, toutefois loin derrière certains modules haut de gamme comme le Renegade Fury G5 de Kingston.
Le Kioxia Exceria Plus G4 respecte le cahier des charges présenté par son constructeur. Sur les benchmarks de CrystalDiskMark, les débits séquentiels affichent une moyenne de 10 397 Mo/s en lecture et 8752 Mo/s en écriture, parfaitement dans les attentes. Ses performances sont quasiment identiques à celles du MP700 Elite de Corsair ; sans grande surprise puisque les deux partagent le même contrôleur et les mêmes puces flash NAND. On était néanmoins en droit d'en attendre un peu plus en qualité de SSD PCIe Gen 5, tant l'interface est capable de débits bien supérieurs.
Il en va de même pour le nombre d'opérations d'entrée/sortie par seconde (IOPS) : sur le test Random4K simulant de nombreuses opérations parallèles, le Kioxia Exceria Plus G4 affiche une constance dans ses performances qui le place au niveau de concurrents pourtant plus onéreux, comme le Samsung 9100 Pro et le WD Black SN8100.
Comme souvent, les différences s'aplanissent en copie manuelle avec une moyenne de 3503 Mo/s en lecture et 2160 Mo/s en écriture sur notre test avec un fichier de 27 Go. Bref, le module reste dans les clous.
Pour son premier SSD PCIe Gen 5, Kioxia ne révolutionne rien, mais ne rate pas le coche pour autant. L'Exceria Plus G4 est un module de stockage efficace, quoiqu'un peu timide lorsqu'il s'agit d'exploiter à fond la bande passante de son interface. Les performances sont présentes, mais forcément limitées eu égard au placement tarifaire d'entrée de gamme.
Les modèles estampillés gaming de Samsung et Sandisk font mieux avec la même interface, pour un prix logiquement plus élevé. À tarif similaire, l'Exceria Plus G4 est supérieur au récent Samsung 990.

articles.title: Eleições 2026: IA é usada para ampliar ataques contra candidatas
articles.text:
A inteligência artificial (IA) ganhou espaço em nova frente das eleições 2026: a produção em escala de imagens ofensivas contra mulheres na política. Um levantamento do projeto MonitorA identificou sinais de uso de IA em 25% das imagens classificadas como ataques ou insultos dirigidos a candidatas no X.
Outros 9% dos casos ficaram em uma zona de incerteza, em que os pesquisadores não conseguiram determinar se houve ou não manipulação por IA.
A análise reuniu 11.137 imagens publicadas em 9.393 comentários em perfis de 132 candidatas. Os conteúdos foram monitorados em dois períodos da campanha: entre 16 e 24 de agosto, na largada da disputa, e de 2 a 11 de setembro, após a crise envolvendo o Supremo Tribunal Federal (STF) e o caso Master.
Ao todo, 660 imagens foram classificadas como ofensivas contra candidatas no X.
IA não busca necessariamente enganar
- O resultado chama atenção porque o uso da IA identificado pelo estudo não está concentrado em deepfakes realistas produzidos para enganar eleitores;
- A maior parte das imagens analisadas é formada por charges, memes, montagens e falsos materiais de campanha criados para humilhar, ridicularizar ou desumanizar as candidatas;
- “Esses usos de montagens e imagens sintéticas de baixa qualidade indicam que, nesses casos, não há necessariamente uma intenção de simular a realidade. A IA aparece, sobretudo, como mais uma ferramenta para a produção e disseminação de conteúdos ofensivos”, resume o relatório;
- O MonitorA divide os conteúdos ofensivos em duas categorias. Os insultos são ofensas com linguagem hostil, mais dura que uma crítica, mas que não recorrem diretamente a marcadores de desigualdade, como gênero, raça ou religião. Foram identificadas 269 imagens nessa categoria;
- Já os ataques buscam inferiorizar e deslegitimar candidatas com base em características associadas a grupos historicamente marginalizados, como gênero, raça, sexualidade, deficiência ou religião. Foram encontrados 391 conteúdos desse tipo;
- Segundo o MonitorA, por seu caráter discriminatório, esses ataques deveriam ser removidos pelas plataformas.
Marina Silva, Sâmia Bomfim e Erika Hilton concentram registros
A candidata que concentrou o maior número de ataques e insultos foi Marina Silva (Rede), com 125 registros ofensivos. Na sequência aparecem Sâmia Bomfim (PSOL), com 111, e Erika Hilton (PSOL), com 109.
Juntas, as três candidatas responderam por quase metade das imagens ofensivas encontradas pela pesquisa.
O levantamento também mostra que as candidatas foram associadas a diferentes tipos de violência.
Entre os conteúdos contra Sâmia Bomfim, predominam ataques gordofóbicos. Segundo o estudo, 70,6% dos ataques direcionados à parlamentar foram classificados nessa categoria.
No caso de Erika Hilton, os ataques são principalmente transfóbicos. Quase metade das ofensas recebidas por ela, 47,9%, foi enquadrada dessa forma. Entre os conteúdos estão referências à negação da identidade de gênero e à reprodução de narrativas transfóbicas.
Marina Silva, por sua vez, aparece principalmente em conteúdos classificados como misóginos, desumanizantes e etaristas. Em algumas imagens, ela é representada como animal ou alienígena, enquanto outras utilizam alterações artificiais para modificar sua aparência e fazê-la parecer mais velha.
Sozinha, Marina foi alvo de 17% de todos os ataques e insultos direcionados às candidatas monitoradas.
Na classificação geral dos ataques, a misoginia apareceu em 99 imagens. Depois vieram gordofobia, com 55; transfobia, com 46; desumanização, com 39; e racismo, com 27.
Tipos mais frequentes de violência envolvendo IA
- Misoginia: 25,3%;
- Gordofobia: 14,1%;
- Transfobia: 11,8%;
- Desumanização: 10,0%;
- Racismo: 6,9%.
Ataques também atingem candidatas da direita
O levantamento encontrou casos envolvendo candidatas de diferentes posições políticas.
Duas candidatas do PL analisadas pelo estudo foram Julia Zanatta e Vanessa da Silva, conhecida como Negona do Bolsonaro.
Zanatta recebeu 76 registros ofensivos durante os períodos analisados. A distribuição, porém, foi desigual: 72 deles apareceram no segundo período, depois da viralização de imagens e vídeos relacionados à candidata.
As ofensas contra ela tinham dois eixos principais: a sexualização, com imagens de biquíni e comentários insinuando interesse sexual, e questionamentos sobre sua identidade política, associando-a a um suposto “falso conservadorismo”.
Vanessa da Silva, por outro lado, foi alvo de 30 imagens ofensivas. Segundo o estudo, 70% continham ataques racistas, incluindo representações relacionadas ao período escravocrata.
O relatório estabelece paralelo entre os dois casos: enquanto Julia aparece em conteúdos com ofensas sexualizantes, Vanessa é retratada como escravizada ou em publicações que a associam a sentimentos de nojo.
Leia mais:
- Starlink será usada pelo TSE em locais remotos nas eleições 2026
- STF amplia acesso gratuito a serviços do TSE e sites de checagem nas eleições
- Eleições 2026: buscas no Google sobre multa eleitoral e venda de bebidas disparam
MonitorA já havia identificado violência contra candidatas no início da campanha
A análise mais recente dá continuidade ao acompanhamento feito pelo MonitorA durante a campanha. Em levantamento realizado entre 16 e 24 de agosto, o projeto identificou 1.318 ataques e insultos contra mulheres no X. Naquele período, Marina Silva concentrou 32% dos registros, seguida por Erika Hilton, com 23%, e Bia Kicis, com 11%.
O MonitorA acompanha padrões de violência política de gênero nas plataformas digitais desde 2020. Em 2026, a quarta edição do projeto reúne InternetLab, Núcleo Jornalismo e Instituto Democracia em Xeque, que participam da coleta, metodologia, análise e produção dos levantamentos.
TSE criou regras para uso de IA nas eleições
O uso de IA durante a campanha também passou a ser tratado de forma específica pela Justiça Eleitoral.
Ao regulamentar as eleições de 2026, o Tribunal Superior Eleitoral (TSE) estabeleceu restrições para conteúdos sintéticos produzidos ou alterados por IA. Entre as regras está a limitação, nas 72 horas anteriores e nas 24 horas posteriores ao pleito, da circulação de novos conteúdos sintéticos que modifiquem imagem, voz ou manifestação de candidatos e pessoas públicas.
A regulamentação também prevê responsabilidade dos provedores em determinadas situações envolvendo conteúdos sintéticos não identificados ou que violem outras regras eleitorais. O TSE ainda proibiu alterações em fotografias, vídeos ou outros registros audiovisuais que contenham cenas de sexo, nudez ou pornografia, em medida relacionada à proteção da dignidade de candidatas e candidatos.
Em setembro, o tribunal também apresentou ferramentas desenvolvidas por empresas de tecnologia para ajudar a proteger a imagem e a voz de mulheres que atuam na política contra usos indevidos de IA.
O estudo do MonitorA mostra, porém, que o uso da tecnologia durante a campanha não se limita à produção de conteúdos que tentam parecer reais. A IA também pode ser utilizada para acelerar a criação de memes, sátiras, montagens e outros materiais ofensivos direcionados a candidatas.
Rodrigo Mozelli é jornalista formado pela Universidade Metodista de São Paulo (UMESP) e, atualmente, é redator do Olhar Digital.

articles.title: SA’s Mission Mobile secures $30.1m funding to help MNOs access more customers - Disrupt Africa
articles.text:
South African mobile technology company Mission Mobile will receive up to ZAR500 million (US$30.1 million) in funding from investment holding company DN Invest (DNI) to help mobile network operators (MNOs) expand their customer base.
Founded in 2023 by Johannesburg-born brothers Tim and Adam Strike, Mission Mobile was created to help network operators build more consistent customer engagement, while at the same time enabling those customers to get more from their mobile spend.
“With more than 80% of South Africa’s mobile connections still on prepaid, a traditional contract remains out of reach for many,” said Tim Strike, co-founder and CEO of Mission Mobile.
“Customers are often spread across multiple SIMs, with little commitment to any one network. That erodes the value of customer relationships for local network providers. It also lessens the purchasing power of their customers and compromises their ability to stay connected.”
Mission Mobile’s solution to this challenge began with Beam, its proprietary technology platform. Beam interprets how people actually earn and spend, rather than relying only on conventional financial assessments. This helps the company identify customers for whom a smartphone offer would be a good fit, but who might otherwise be overlooked by traditional providers.
Mission Mobile has since turned that capability into a model offered to customers through MNO retail outlets. Its approach is grounded in a deep understanding of both the local market, and the challenge operators face in serving a wider range of customers.
“Our technology helps us connect customers with smartphone offers that suit their needs and give them more value from their mobile spend,” said Tim. “This enables network providers to serve people who might previously have been out of reach, while helping customers stay connected and active on the same SIM. Ultimately, this creates more predictable engagement, stronger loyalty and greater long-term value for networks and their customers.”
The startup has now secured up to ZAR500 million in funding from DNI, which will enable it to expand its model, helping MNOs serve a broader customer base, while giving more people access to smartphones and cost-effective connectivity. It will extend the startup’s customer reach and support the development of further propositions for network providers.
“DNI invests in the people behind the businesses,” said Mick Silke, CEO of finco at DNI. “Tim, Adam and their team recognised an opportunity to help mobile network operators serve millions more people and built the technology to make that possible. The commercial opportunity is considerable, but so is the potential impact on people’s lives—greater value from their hard-earned money and the ability to stay connected. Businesses that can achieve both are rare, and they are exactly the ones we look to support.”
