articles.title: Rivian's R2 just helped it set a new sales record | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Rivian sold more electric vehicles than ever in the third quarter, thanks in large part to the launch of its new, more affordable R2 SUV.
The company said Friday morning that it built 19,751 vehicles and delivered 19,248. That’s roughly 45% more than it delivered in the same period last year.
While Rivian didn’t break out how many of those were R2 SUVs, this was the first full quarter of sales of the new vehicle after it launched in June. The company said Friday that it will release its full third-quarter financial results on October 29.
Rivian has big plans for the R2, which currently starts at just under $60,000. The company is betting that it will sell between 20,000 to 25,000 R2 vehicles by the end of the year, which would make it one of the fastest-selling EVs in U.S. history — second only to Tesla’s Model Y. Rivian also plans to make cheaper models available that will cost as low as around $45,000.
If Rivian hits those numbers, the company believes it can sell between 65,000 and 70,000 vehicles this year, including its R1 lineup of vehicles and its commercial electric van. That would be its best sales year ever, as the company has spent the last few years stuck at around the 50,000-vehicles-sold mark.
Rivian is currently building the R2 at its factory in Normal, Illinois, where it recently expanded the production space to accommodate the new SUV. But Rivian is also building a brand new factory outside Atlanta, Georgia, where it expects to be able to build as many as 300,000 vehicles per year in the near future, with the option to expand that capacity down the road.
Rivian needs the R2 to sell well in order to staunch years of heavy losses, due in part to the company’s expensive infrastructure required to support this mass-market vehicle. But Rivian has also signed a deal with Uber to make robotaxi versions of the R2 SUV. Rivian believes robotaxis represent such a big potential market that, in March, the company pushed back its goal of reaching profitability in 2027 to invest more money into autonomy.

articles.title: Kein Ende in Sicht: Warum die Speicherkrise noch viele Jahre andauern könnte
articles.text:
Kein Ende in Sicht: Warum die Speicherkrise noch viele Jahre andauern könnte
Die Speicherkrise ist für Kund:innen mehr als ärgerlich. PC-Komponenten wie Arbeitsspeicher sind seit Monaten deutlich teurer. Und auch bei Smartphones, Motherboards und Co. ziehen die Preise stetig an, weil die Herstellungskosten steigen. Die Gewinner der RAM-Krise sind hingegen Unternehmen wie Micron, einer der größten Hersteller für Speicherchips. Jetzt hat Micron einen neuen Quartalsbericht veröffentlicht, der keine Hoffnung auf eine Zukunft ohne RAM-Not macht.
RAM-Krise: Keine Aussicht auf Besserung
In dem Quartalsbericht von Micron traf Sanjay Mehrotra, CEO des Unternehmens, mehrere Aussagen über die Zukunft und die RAM-Krise: „So stark das Fiskaljahr 2026 auch war, wir erwarten, dass 2027 noch besser wird. Die Nachfrage der Industrie ist seit unserem letzten Bericht angestiegen und wir erwarten, dass die Bedingungen für die RAM- und Speicherversorgung 2027 und 2028 noch knapper werden als sie es schon 2026 waren.“
Mehrotra fügt hinzu: „Selbst mit den Plänen für zusätzlichen DRAM‑Reinraumplatz […] haben wir keinerlei Idee, wann Nachfrage und Angebot wieder in eine Balance geraten.“ Das liegt laut dem Micron-CEO unter anderem daran, dass die Nachfrage im KI-Bereich weiterhin steigt: „KI-Anwendungen, egal ob Open-Source- oder Closed-Source-Modelle, laufen auf einer Vielzahl von Kundenplattformen. Diese Plattformen teilen alle eine wichtige Charakteristik. Ihr Nutzerversprechen wird durch die Leistung und Kapazität von Speicher und RAM verstärkt.“
Auch wenn der Fall eintreten sollte, dass die KI-Blase platzt, sieht Micron noch keinerlei Entspannung für den Markt. Dann hätte das Unternehmen immer noch das Interesse von Herstellern von „physischen KI“-Gadgets wie autonomen Fahrzeugen und Robotern. „Mit dem erwarteten Anstieg von Einheiten und Speicherkapazität, wird physische KI bis zum Ende dieses Jahrzehnts zu einem signifikanten Treiber für die Nachfrage von Speicher und RAM“, heißt es im Bericht.
Für Endkund:innen von Smartphones und PC-Komponenten bedeutet dieser Ausblick, dass sich auch in den kommenden Jahren nur wenig an den steigenden Preisen ändern dürfte. Einige Tech-Hersteller gehen sogar davon aus, dass die RAM-Krise mehrere Unternehmen zu Schließungen zwingen könnte, weil sie die Preise für ihre Produkte nicht unendlich erhöhen können, ohne das Interesse der Konsument:innen zu verlieren.

articles.title: Chip Industry Week In Review
articles.text:
Chip Industry Week In Review
                    
    
    
                            
						
Autonomous workflow design; CFETs push scaling beyond 10 angstroms; onsemi-Synaptics deal revised; physical AI M&A and funding; AI data centers drive new power/packaging investments; new Spectre-v2 attack targets JIT compilers; photonics moves closer to compute; quantum HW; false base station risks; 88k engineers needed.
					
				 
				
				
					
Top of the Week
- Synopsys unveiled a portfolio of domain-specific long-horizon agents that can reason, plan, and execute multi-step engineering workflows across verification, system validation, implementation, analog, manufacturing, simulation and analysis. Synopsys also inked a multi-year agreement with OpenAI to develop GPT-Synopsys, a specialized model optimized to use its EDA tools for semiconductor design workflows.
- Semiconductor Engineering released its Photonics eBook, an in-depth look at the technologies, applications, and ongoing research that will be needed to address the growing bandwidth problem in data centers and semiconductor packages.
- Lam Research proposed a self-aligned CFET architecture (right) that could extend CMOS scaling below 10 angstroms. Its digital-twin modeling produced a 0.0094 μm² 6T SRAM bit cell, which is 52.7% smaller than N3 technology, while maintaining at least a 10 nm overlay window across critical contact layers.
- TSMC is reportedly evaluating a semiconductor manufacturing investment in Texas that would expand its U.S. production footprint beyond its $265B Arizona buildout, per Bloomberg.
- S. Korea’s semiconductor exports surged over 262% year over year to a record $60B in September, driven by stronger memory demand, higher shipment volumes and rising memory prices.
Threats and defenses
- VUSec and SSSA researchers uncovered Branch Target Reuse, a new Spectre-v2 attack targeting just-in-time compilers. They demonstrated an end-to-end Linux attack that can leak arbitrary memory — including a root password hash — even with existing Spectre defenses enabled. Hardware vendors said existing mitigation mechanisms can address BTR, with protections deployed through software.
- Nvidia launched its Open Agent Safety Platform, combining open-source software with hardware-based controls for agentic AI security. Its Sentry reference design runs on BlueField-4 DPUs to monitor agent behavior and enforce security policies independently in silicon, quarantining agents that move outside defined boundaries. Cadence is integrating the platform with its AI Super Agents to add runtime controls around autonomous chip-design workflows.
Physical AI
- AMD plans to acquire World Labs, which develops spatial-intelligence AI models that simulate interactive 3D environments for robotics. The $8.2B all-stock deal is expected to close by the end of 2026.
- SiMa.ai raised $150M to develop physical AI solutions, including silicon with 1,000+ TOPS and an agentic software environment.
- Physical AI is pushing more intelligence into edge devices, where systems must turn sensor data into real-time action, increasing demands for compute, memory, connectivity, power efficiency, and security.
Capacity
Fig. 2: Infineon’s new backend manufacturing hub in Bangkok, Thailand
Memory
- Micron says memory supply will remain tight through 2028, with more than 75% of its 2027 output already committed. It also said 2027 HBM pricing will be significantly higher than 2026 levels. Micron reported record Q4 revenue of $54B, up from $11B a year earlier.
- HBM is expected to consume nearly 30% of DRAM manufacturers’ wafer capacity in 2027, up from about 20% currently, a Samsung executive told Reuters.
- Teradyne introduced its Magnum E2 high-speed memory test system, supporting next-generation LPDDR6 and DDR6, as well as GDDR7 and NAND flash for growing AI and HPC memory requirements.
Photonics
- JEDEC published the industry’s first silicon photonics reliability standard, establishing common qualification and reliability requirements as optical interconnects scale for AI and data-center systems.
- Counterpoint says network bottlenecks are becoming a bigger constraint on AI accelerator performance, with GPUs spending roughly 12.5% of their time waiting on the network in some workloads. The firm expects near-packaged optics to begin sampling in late 2026 or early 2027, followed by CPO as AI systems demand faster, more power-efficient scale-up interconnects.

Global
Americas
- California now exempts certain chemical mixtures containing 70% or less gamma-butyrolactone (GBL) from state permitting, reporting, and other regulatory requirements. GBL is used as a solvent in semiconductor photoresists. Controls on pure GBL remain.
- Lam Research opened a 470k-sq.ft. logistics and supply hub in Livermore, California.
- S. Korea and the U.S. are advancing a $22B gas-fired power project in Texas, part of a broader Korea-U.S. strategic investment package of up to $350B. The 6.47-GW project is aimed at meeting rising power demand from semiconductor plants and AI data centers.
Europe
- Fraunhofer IAF announced newly launched research initiatives in AI-assisted chip design and chips for AI applications, including AI-accelerated CMOS design and hardware for edge AI. The institute is also showcasing its III-V semiconductor pilot-line capabilities for heterogeneous integration and chip manufacturing.
- Global Electronics Association and the Fraunhofer Group for Microelectronics signed an agreement to accelerate industrial adoption of advanced packaging technologies.
Asia
- Semifive inked a deal with Mobilint to develop a robotics AI processor under South Korea’s K-On-Device AI Semiconductor program.
- Air Liquide will invest more than US$193M in production units supplying ultra-pure gases to support the expansion of an existing advanced logic-chip fab in southern Japan.
Reports and Deals
More deals
- Infineon will supply SiC power devices for Eaton’s MVSST 2.0 solid-state transformer platform, designed to support emerging 800 VDC architectures for high-density AI data centers.
- onsemi revised its planned acquisition of Synaptics to a $5.7B all-cash deal, offering $123 per share, after Synaptics received an unsolicited competing proposal. The original June agreement was valued at approximately $7B.
- Amazon broadened its use of Synopsys products to include application-optimized silicon IP for custom chips and AWS infrastructure, with the companies also planning custom agentic-AI capabilities.
- Anthropic’s IPO filing revealed that it is the customer behind Broadcom’s previously disclosed AI compute-financing arrangement of up to $42B.
- Applied Materials added Kioxia and Besi as partners at its $5B EPIC Center, expanding work on next-gen memory and advanced packaging.
- Samsung will invest a combined $1B in Helix Digital Infrastructure, an integrated AI infrastructure spanning hyperscale data centers, power generation and transmission, and fiber-optic networks.
- Tanaka began a collaboration with TNO/CITC to develop and evaluate next-generation semiconductor-packaging materials, including silver- and copper-based adhesive pastes for die and clip bonding.
- DeepSeek will develop programming tools optimized for Huawei‘s AI chips, including compute and communication libraries, per Reuters.
Fundings, IPO
- CScale exited stealth with $145M in funding to commercialize an optical interconnect for AI scale-up that is architected to contain optical failures without interrupting compute.
- Efficient Computer raised $97M to ship its energy-efficient general-purpose processor in volume and scale the architecture to data center-class performance.
- Volantis raised $88M for its optical interconnect that uses integrated micro-VCSELs to connect large numbers of memory chips into a unified pool for AI inference.
- Zenithon AI raised $10M to develop AI world models for extreme physics applications, including semiconductor manufacturing.
- SK hynix‘s U.S. subsidiary Solidigm is pondering an IPO, reports Reuters. SK says nothing has been decided.
Reports
- Revenue across the broader semiconductor manufacturing ecosystem, including foundries, IDMs, packaging and test, reached a record $96.6B in 2Q26, up 25% YoY, reports Counterpoint.
- Conventional DRAM contract prices are expected to rise 10% to 15% in 4Q26 and NAND flash prices 15% to 20%, per TrendForce. Enterprise SSD bit demand is projected to grow more than 80% in 2026.
- Bain says AI has reversed the long-running advantage of software over hardware, with semiconductor and hardware stocks growing at a 24% compound annual rate from 2020 to 2026 versus 6% for software.
- N. American EMS and PCB shipments for August 2026 (Global Electronics)
New Technologies
Test, measurement, and failure analysis
- Keysight introduced a 20 GHz dual-channel analog signal generator with ultra-low noise, calibrated output power, and software mode switching to optimize performance across different applications.
- Hamamatsu Photonics developed an inverted emission microscope for failure analysis of advanced packages including HBM, AI chiplets, and 2.5D/3D devices.
Compute, embedded, and engineering tools
- AMD started sampling a Versal adaptive SoC in a space-grade organic lidless package designed to support missions lasting up to 15 years. AMD also introduced an agentic AI assistant to accelerate the embedded development flow.
- Siemens announced several updates to its Simcenter Testlab engineering software, including improvements to how the system aids structural dynamics, system NVH prediction, and AI-ready data preparation workflows.
Connectivity and memory
Adoptions & wins
- Siemens said naval engineering company Caponnetto Hueber used its digital-twin technology to improve hydrodynamic performance and sustainability in vessel design.
Research
University of Tokyo, NTU and others grew boron carbon nitride as a high-performance p-type semiconductor, with hole mobility up to 100 cm²/V·s, on-current above 0.9 mA/μm, and on/off ratios up to 10⁸.
Purdue and UCLA “experimentally quantify the impact of Cu microstructure on the TSV-induced residual stress within silicon.”
Stockholm University researchers developed an electrically tunable superconducting diode that allows supercurrent to flow in one direction while suppressing it in the other, without an applied magnetic field.
Yale and EPFL researchers each reported advances in integrated lasers, with Yale demonstrating an Nd laser and amplifier platform with a 2.9 μW threshold, 46.6 dB gain and more than 12 dBm output, and EPFL developed a silicon-nitride laser that remains self-injection locked across its full drive-current range, with sub-10-Hz linewidths and mode-hop-free 1.5-GHz chirps.
Security
Fraunhofer completed silicon validation of its RISC-V Secure Element and made the OpenTitan-based design available as licensable security IP for SoCs, ASICs and chiplets. It integrates HW root-of-trust functions including secure boot, key storage and device identity.
Vulnerabilities and guidance
- NIST released a draft 5G security white paper on false base stations, finding that 5G standards have reduced privacy and location-tracking risks, but devices can still be vulnerable to denial-of-service attacks.
- NSA set new post-quantum cryptography requirements for National Security Systems, including quantum-resistant support for new commercial systems beginning in 2027 and phaseout of incompatible legacy systems by 2030.
- A major data breach at the Pentagon’s Defense Manpower Data Center exposed the unencrypted personal information of over 3 million people. The breach came as a result of a security vulnerability in the agency’s file-sharing system.
- Citrix disclosed eight new vulnerabilities affecting its Citrix NetScaler ADC and Citrix NetScaler Gateway products, including two actively exploited critical, zero-day vulnerabilities that can enable remote code execution, according to CISA. All of CISA’s alerts for the week can be found here.
- A security researcher uncovered an access-control vulnerability in Flock Safety’s infrastructure that exposed ArcGIS location data, allowing him to map more than 300,000 Flock-associated surveillance devices across the U.S.
- PWC released a report finding that 84% of security and finance leaders expect cyber budgets to rise over the next year amid rising AI threats.
Security technical papers and reports
Vehicles, Batteries
Architecture shift
- The shift toward AI-defined vehicles is pushing automotive compute, memory bandwidth, data movement, and validation requirements higher. Automakers are weighing centralized versus distributed architectures as increasingly data-heavy AI workloads strain in-vehicle networks, power budgets, and long-term safety verification.
Automotive chips
AVs, EVs
Vehicle technical papers
Quantum
Hardware
- Alice & Bob proposed a faster approach to stabilizing microwave resonator cat-qubits in superconducting quantum systems for compact designs that generate less heat.
- Xanadu and Bluefors are developing a modular cryogenic system for utility-scale photonic quantum computers, aimed at cooling large arrays of single-photon detectors without requiring industrial-scale cryogenic plants.
- QCi introduced its Dirac-3S photonic quantum system, built for large optimization problems. The system has been demonstrated with up to 9,980 variables, versus 949 for the current Dirac-3.
QC training/ infrastructure
- New Mexico opened the Roadrunner Quantum Lab in Albuquerque, giving quantum startups shared access to dilution refrigerators, a multi-node quantum network, testbeds, and demonstration facilities. California announced a $30M investment in quantum and deep-space research, alongside new quantum-workforce initiatives.
- XeedQ will install a 4-qubit room-temperature quantum computer at Skyview High School in December, which Fairfax County Public Schools says will be the first operational quantum computer in a K-12 school.

SEMI says semiconductor workforce shortages are increasingly concentrated in advanced packaging and experienced manufacturing leadership. The U.S. could need 88,000 new engineers by 2029, while nearly 30% of Europe’s semiconductor workforce is expected to retire by 2030.
University of Arkansas launched the Arkansas Research Institute for Electronics Systems to expand semiconductor research and train undergraduate and graduate students.
A second federal judge blocked enforcement of the $100K H-1B fee, ruling that immigration agencies failed to follow required notice-and-comment procedures. The Sept. 30 order also prevents agencies from enforcing the fee under the administration’s September extension while the ruling remains in effect.
ETH Zürich professor Onur Mutlu has made his 2026 Digital Design & Computer Architecture course freely available online. The course starts with transistor and digital-logic fundamentals and progresses through Verilog, microarchitecture, pipelining, out-of-order execution, branch prediction, GPUs, memory systems, caches, and emerging computing architectures.

articles.title: NVIDIA DGX Spark 64GB Gives Developers More Ways to Build and Scale Local AI
articles.text:
Local AI is becoming more useful by the token.
As AI agents move from experiments into everyday development, increasingly capable open models are shrinking to fit on more devices, giving builders more to run locally.
Coming this month, NVIDIA DGX Spark will be available with 64GB of unified memory from top manufacturer partners — Acer, ASUS, Dell, Gigabyte, HP and MSI — giving developers, researchers and AI enthusiasts a new configuration with DGX OS and the NVIDIA AI software stack ready to use from day one.
The new SKU runs capable local agents on device — privately, without cloud dependency. And when workloads grow, two units can cluster together via NVIDIA Sync Cluster Assistant without any additional setup.
A New Starting Point for Personal AI Supercomputing
DGX Spark combines NVIDIA Grace Blackwell compute, unified memory, NVIDIA ConnectX-7 networking and an NVIDIA CUDA-accelerated AI software stack in one system. It’s a complete local AI platform for agents, inference, fine-tuning, data science and edge development.
The compact, personal AI supercomputer provides a place to experiment with models and developers’ own data without turning to a cloud instance for every task.
The new 64GB configuration, available exclusively from manufacturer partners, keeps the platform at an accessible price point while retaining the GB10 Grace Blackwell Superchip, DGX OS and full NVIDIA AI software stack — same as the 128GB model. It supports up to 100-billion-parameter models and the agentic applications built on them, fully on device.
Two 64GB units clustered together don’t just double the memory. In NVIDIA’s Qwen 3.8 27B test, two clustered 64 GB systems delivered up to 1.7x performance compared with a single system, with room to keep scaling as workloads demand.
DGX Spark ships ready for agent development from day one — NVIDIA Agent Toolkit, CUDA-X AI libraries, Nemotron open models, and popular runtimes like Ollama, vLLM, and PyTorch with CUDA are all supported out of the box. Developers can go from power-on to running models in minutes.
Blender is among the first major creator application providers to support the platform, with a prebuilt, downloadable installer coming soon.
Scale Up With NVIDIA Sync Cluster Assistant
Developers can start with the memory their projects need today and build on a platform designed to seamlessly scale multi-node clusters for larger workloads as their pipelines grow.
Every DGX Spark ships with a built-in NVIDIA ConnectX-7 NIC right out of the box. Plus, two units can connect directly with a QSFP cable, pooling their memory to 128GB and expanding model support to up to 200 billion parameters while delivering twice the memory bandwidth and up to 1.7x the performance.
The NVIDIA Sync app configures this multi-node cluster seamlessly. The cluster assistant feature detects connected units, validates device configuration and configures the ConnectX-7 network, so developers can focus on their work rather than the infrastructure. Every node runs the same NVIDIA software stack, so nothing needs to be reconfigured when scaling from one unit to two.
And coming at the end of the month, NVIDIA Sync Model Launcher makes running local AI as simple as clicking a few buttons. Developers can download and launch Qwen3.8 27B on a single DGX Spark system or a cluster, with NVIDIA Sync configuring the model to run across connected devices and making it accessible from users’ laptops. The launcher will also set up OpenCode to use the model, so developers can start coding in their browser.
Developer Use Cases on DGX Spark
The new DGX Spark 64GB configuration supports practical work from day one. With up to 100-billion-parameter models running entirely on device, developers and enthusiasts can start with a single system for models that fit within its memory, or connect multiple DGX Spark systems with NVIDIA Sync Cluster Assistant for workloads that need more memory and compute.
Here are three workflow examples:
- Run an AI agent around the clock: Keep a coding or research agent running on DGX Spark, ready to review code, analyze documents or carry out multistep tasks. A cluster provides additional capacity for larger models, longer context windows or multiple agents working at once.
- Power AI apps on your everyday PC: Run a language- or image-generation model on DGX Spark while using an agent or creative application on laptops or desktops. DGX Spark handles the model inference, freeing PCs for other work.
- Scale when the work grows: When a single task outgrows one unit — running a larger model, a longer context window or concurrent agent requests — two DGX Spark 64GB systems connected over the 200 GbE fabric via NVIDIA Sync Cluster Assistant pool their memory to 128GB. The same workflow that ran on one unit scales to two without reconfiguring the software environment.
Get Started With DGX Spark
DGX Spark 64GB is available from Acer, ASUS, Dell, Gigabyte, HP and MSI on Friday, Oct. 23, starting at $4,999.
To get started:
- Download a supported inference framework — llama.cpp, Ollama, vLLM or LM Studio.
- Download the recommended local model for the workflow.
- To scale to two units, connect them via their NVIDIA ConnectX-7 ports and launch NVIDIA Sync Cluster Assistant — it configures the network and routes workloads automatically.
For agentic AI playbooks on DGX Spark, visit the NemoClaw, OpenClaw, Hermes Agent and OpenShell pages on build.nvidia.com.
#ICYMI: More Updates From NVIDIA Local AI
Explore playbooks on build.nvidia.com/spark for DGX Spark. The following playbooks are coming soon to 64GB devices:
- Serve LLMs With vLLM
- Run OpenClaw With a Local LLM
- Connect Multiple DGX Sparks for Distributed Workloads
New Windows PCs powered by NVIDIA RTX Spark are coming this month from Acer, ASUS, Dell, HP, Lenovo, Microsoft and MSI. Sign up for the RTX Spark newsletter to receive future updates.
Alibaba’s Qwen-Image-2.1 brings image generation and editing together in a lightweight, open-weight model. It runs locally on NVIDIA RTX GPUs, DGX Spark and DGX Station, giving creators more ways to create and refine images on their own hardware.
Follow NVIDIA RTX Spark on X, Instagram, TikTok and Facebook — and stay informed by subscribing to the NVIDIA Local AI newsletter. Follow NVIDIA Workstation on LinkedIn and X.

articles.title: Dots get up in Muse’s business
articles.text:
OpenAI’s answer to Muse arrived this week, and it looks a whole lot like Muse dressed up in a suit and tie. Dots is a business-first product — for now, at least — costing a minimum of $100 per month. And sure, you can make a cute little Dot character, just like you can make a cute little Muse character. But OpenAI’s early marketing is all about how you can use it to do Business Things: launch websites, reschedule calls, build slide decks for board meetings. Muse, on the other hand, keeps reminding me to buy a jacket I looked at.
Dots get up in Muse’s business
On The Vergecast: OpenAI’s new agentic assistant, Trump’s attempt at AI safety, and lots of gadgets.
This week on The Vergecast, we’re talking about Dots and the current state of agentic assistants. Our conversation quickly turns back to Muse, which we’ve all been trying out to varying degrees of success. David Imel put it in charge of his Facebook Marketplace listings. Nilay Patel had it sort through his junk email. It managed to do both, and it managed to make us uncomfortable in the process.
Watch | Listen | Get ad-free
On the topic of trusting AI, we had to discuss this week’s AI compact, where tech leaders gathered at the White House to sign a “morally binding” agreement to police themselves and make sure their models don’t go off the rails. We’re not really sure this one’s going to do much.
After that, it’s a big round of gadget news: a wild new Huawei phone-slash-camera, a polished new suite of Kindles, and rumors of the forthcoming HomePad. Then we head into everyone’s favorite podcast within a podcast, and finally over to the Lightning Round, where we’re talking America’s new chatbot, Reddit further limiting access, Cybercabs, and more.
If you want to learn more about any of the stories we discussed this week, you can check out the links below.

articles.title: Rivian issues R2 recall for poorly tightened battery packs | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Rivian has issued a recall for its R2 SUV after the company discovered that fasteners on its high-voltage battery pack might not be properly tightened, which can cause a loss of power while driving.
The company says only around 14 vehicles may have been affected, and that it will repair or replace damaged components on customer vehicles as needed. Rivian told TechCrunch that all of the affected vehicles are at service centers “being inspected to properly torque the fastener or replace damaged components at no cost to customers.”
This is the second recall Rivian has issued for the R2, which started shipping to customers this year. It’s an all-important vehicle for the company, as it’s the first Rivian EV meant for a mass market and is supposed to help it reach profitability for the first time. The first R2 recall, issued last month, had to do with the visibility of the backup camera and was addressed with a software update.
In a filing, the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) said Rivian first spotted the defect on September 17. A “manufacturing operator” at the company’s Normal, Illinois factory noticed one of the fasteners had been “under torqued” by an “automated station” on the assembly line. The company investigated and reprogrammed the station to reject “improperly torqued fasteners.”
Rivian told the safety regulator that it “is not aware of any customer reports, accidents, injuries, or fatalities
related to this issue.” Some Reddit users, along with RivianTrackr, a blog that follows the company closely, reported about the issue late last month. One owner said Rivian’s service department told them to stop driving immediately, and the company towed the vehicle.
Rivian has set an aggressive goal for the launch of the R2. The company has said it plans to ship between 20,000 and 25,000 of them by the end of this year. With deliveries starting in June, that would make it one of the fastest launches of a new EV in the U.S. market if Rivian pulls it off. The company is supposed to be adding a second production shift to hit those numbers, and has said early demand is strong for the new, more affordable SUV.
This story has been updated with information from Rivian.

articles.title: Test de l'iPhone 18 Pro Max : si puissant, si endurant et si cher — Frandroid
articles.text:
Pas d’iPhone 18 ni d’iPhone Duo en cette rentrée de septembre. Pour lancer sa nouvelle gamme, Apple s’est concentré sur les modèles Pro. Si d’extérieur, ils ne se distinguent des iPhone 17 Pro que par leurs nouveaux coloris, c’est dans leurs entrailles qu’Apple a poussé les potards avec des composants peaufinés pour une expérience utilisateur nettoyée des défauts de la génération précédente. Chauffe, autonomie, recharge, photo de nuit, tous ces points ont été revus et corrigés. Les iPhone 18 Pro peaufinent une formule déjà connue et gagnent en maturité.
Après avoir testé en long et en large le plus petit des deux, nous passons à l’iPhone 18 Pro Max. Je joue avec ce dernier depuis bientôt deux semaines, ce qui m’a laissé le temps d’apprécier les différences qu’il entretient avec l’iPhone 17 Pro Max que j’utilise depuis un an.
Apple a largement réduit les différences entre ses deux iPhone Pro. Jusqu’aux iPhone 15 Pro, le Pro Max avait un meilleur téléobjectif. C’est fini depuis les iPhone 16 Pro. Il ne reste que trois vraies différences : les dimensions, l’écran et la batterie.
Aussi, ne vais-je m’attarder ici que sur ces trois aspects. Pour tout le reste, je vous invite à lire le test très exhaustif de l’iPhone 18 Pro par Ulrich.
    Pour aller plus loin
Test de l’iPhone 18 Pro : le meilleur iPhone est aussi le plus prudent
            
Apple iPhone 18 Pro MaxFiche technique
| Modèle | Apple iPhone 18 Pro Max | 
|---|---|
| Dimensions | 78 mm x 163,4 mm x 8,75 mm | 
| Interface constructeur | iOS | 
| Taille de l’écran | 6,9 pouces | 
| Définition | 2 868 x 1 320 pixels | 
| Densité de pixels | 460 ppp | 
| Technologie | OLED | 
| SoC | Apple A20 Pro | 
| Puce graphique | Apple GPU | 
| Stockage interne | 256, 512, 1000, 2000 Go | 
| Appareil photo (dorsal) | Capteur 1 : 48 Capteur 2 : 48 Capteur 3 : 48 Mp | 
| Capteur photo frontal | 18 Mp | 
| Définition enregistrement vidéo | 4K | 
| Wi-fi | Wi-Fi 7 (be) | 
| Bluetooth | 6.0 | 
| 5G | Oui | 
| NFC | Oui | 
| Type de connecteur | USB Type-C | 
| Poids | 249 g | 
| Couleurs | Noir, Argent, Blanc | 
|  | Fiche produit | 
Apple iPhone 18 Pro MaxDesign
L’iPhone 18 Pro Max peut accueillir les coques du 17 Pro Max. C’est un fait, je l’ai moi-même vérifié avec mon ancienne coque, ça matche parfaitement. Apple me disait pourtant le contraire. En réalité, c’est le plateau photo qui est un peu plus épais sur l’iPhone 18 Pro Max, mais il reste parfaitement protégé.
Les dimensions (longueur, largeur, épaisseur) sont strictement les mêmes que celles du 17 Pro Max, soit 163,4 x 78 x 8,75 mm. Seul le poids diffère. On passe de 231 g à 249 g, soit 18 g de plus. Une différence plus prononcée que sur l’iPhone 18 Pro.
Elle est notamment due à la chambre à vapeur, qui s’est largement étalée sur ces modèles. Il y a également la batterie qui prend plus de place avec sa capacité étendue.
Ce surpoids se sent lorsqu’on a les deux téléphones en main, mais à l’usage, cela ne m’a pas plus dérangé que cela. On reste sur un très grand smartphone, déjà difficile à utiliser à une main.
Apple iPhone 18 Pro MaxÉcran
De 6,3 pouces pour l’iPhone 18 Pro, on passe à 6,9 pouces sur l’iPhone 18 Pro Max. La définition change en conséquence avec 2868 x 1320 pixels. La densité est identique : 460 ppp.
Rien de plus à dire sur l’écran : il est très bien calibré et assez lumineux pour toutes les situations.
Pour plus de détails, on vous renvoie vers la partie écran du test de l’iPhone 18 Pro.
Apple iPhone 18 Pro MaxPerformances
Même SoC A20 Pro sur les deux 18 Pro, mais le Pro Max étant plus grand, il a une chambre à vapeur plus vaste. Il n’en fallait pas plus pour que j’aie envie de relancer tout mon protocole performances dessus.
Je n’ai pas eu tort. On a un léger écart entre les deux Pro, à l’avantage du 18 Pro Max.
Globalement, ça se matérialise surtout sur la partie graphique, avec des scores GPU plus généreux sur 3DMark et Geekbench pour le 18 Pro Max.
Attention, l’écart reste mince : 1,3 % de performances en plus pour l’iPhone 18 Pro Max sur l’ensemble des tests. Sa chambre à vapeur plus grande l’aide à mieux contenir sa température, ce qui explique ce léger surplus de puissance.
    Pour aller plus loin
Test de l’iPhone 18 Pro : le meilleur iPhone est aussi le plus prudent
            
Apple iPhone 18 Pro MaxLogiciel
Côté logiciel, l’iPhone 18 Pro Max offre rigoureusement la même expérience que son petit frère sous iOS 27. On a un système particulièrement stable, fluide, sans les habituels petits bugs de jeunesse. En revanche, le constat reste identique côté intelligence artificielle : malgré la puissance brute de la puce sous le capot, l’absence de Siri AI en France laisse toujours un goût d’inachevé, sans compter les quelques ratés persistants de la dictée vocale.
L’expérience étant 100 % similaire d’un modèle à l’autre, nous vous renvoyons directement vers la partie logicielle de notre test complet de l’iPhone 18 Pro pour retrouver notre avis détaillé.
Apple iPhone 18 Pro MaxPhoto
L’iPhone 18 Pro Max partage à l’identique son équipement photo avec l’iPhone 18 Pro. On y retrouve la grande nouveauté matérielle de l’année : ce diaphragme mécanique à ouverture variable (f/1,48 à f/4) sur le capteur principal.
Si cette variation s’avère anecdotique en photo de jour (le mode auto boudant f/2,8 pour favoriser f/1,48), la grande ouverture change en revanche la donne la nuit en captant bien plus de lumière, sans parler de son réel intérêt cinématique en vidéo pour fermer à f/4 sans filtre ND.
En revanche, le téléobjectif 4x commence sérieusement à accuser le coup face aux concurrents Android dès qu’on dépasse le recadrage 8x. Les résultats et les capteurs étant strictement les mêmes, vous pouvez retrouver tous nos clichés comparatifs, nos mesures et notre verdict complet dans la partie photo et vidéo de notre test de l’iPhone 18 Pro.
Apple iPhone 18 Pro MaxBatterie
L’iPhone 18 Pro Max est donc plus lourd, mais c’est pour la bonne cause, comme on l’a vu plus haut. En effet, côté batterie, il gagne 11 % de capacité en plus pour atteindre 5391 mAh. Une donnée non fournie par Apple, mais que l’on obtient grâce à la base de données européenne qui oblige Apple à la leur communiquer.
Selon sa fiche EPREL, l’iPhone 18 Pro Max tient 62 heures au test d’endurance européen, soit 9 heures de plus que l’iPhone 17 Pro Max.
De mon côté, j’ai pris mes mesures. J’ai évidemment attendu que l’iPhone termine son indexation. L’an dernier, en usage classique, avec entre 2 et 3 heures d’écran par jour, j’avais tenu plus d’un jour et demi, le smartphone tombant à 1 % à 16 h le deuxième jour.
Avec l’iPhone 18 Pro Max, je suis allé plus loin ! Certes, sans GPS cette fois, mais sans non plus activer le mode économie d’énergie, contrairement à mon test de l’iPhone 17 Pro Max. Côté usage, c’était toujours classique avec notamment du streaming, du jeu vidéo, du scroll, des appels et de la photo/vidéo. Au final, j’ai pu traverser un week-end en prenant l’iPhone le samedi à 7h et me coucher le dimanche soir avec encore 15% de batterie à 23h30. Il en avait encore sous le pied.
| Paramètre / Critère | iPhone 17 Pro Max | iPhone 18 Pro Max | Évolution | 
| Capacité nominale de la batterie | 4 823 mAh | 5 391 mAh | +568 mAh / +11,8 % | 
| Autonomie par cycle (test normalisé UE) | 53 h 00 min | 62 h 00 min | +9 h / +17,0 % | 
| Durabilité en cycles (paramètres par défaut) | 1 000 cycles | 1 000 cycles | Identique | 
Une belle performance que j’ai pu confirmer en streaming vidéo. En suivant mon protocole — Wi-Fi uniquement, avec écran calé à 250 nits et volume à 50 % — les 2h30 de lecture de À l’Ouest rien de nouveau sur Netflix n’a consommé que 6 % de l’autonomie globale. C’est ridiculement bas. En comparaison, un smartphone Android bon en la matière épuise 9 % de sa batterie. Ceci dit, je ne pouvais espérer moins, l’iPhone 17e étant déjà très bien placé avec -7% pour sa part sur le même test.
En jeu, j’ai lancé une session de Genshin Impact en suivant les mêmes critères. Les paramètres graphiques sont poussés à fond, sauf le framerate. Le 120 fps est disponible, mais pour être comparé aux Android, je me suis limité à 60 fps. Là, excellente surprise : 8 % de batterie consommés en une heure de jeu. C’est bien moins que la moyenne générale. Pour ne rien gâcher, c’est même mieux que l’iPhone 17 Pro Max qui consomme, lui, 11 % de sa batterie sur la même durée.
Attention tout de même, j’ai activé le MetalFX, une technologie d’Apple qui augmente les performances en faisant calculer le jeu dans une résolution plus basse, puis en reconstruisant une image plus grande et plus nette avant son affichage. Grosso modo, l’équivalent du DLSS de Nvidia.
Cela allège la charge du SoC et économise la batterie. Sans le MetalFX, on passe à 17% utilisés en une heure de Genshin sur l’iPhone 18 Pro Max. La différence est énorme.
Charge
La charge aussi a été améliorée. Apple promet 50 % de batterie en environ 15 minutes sur l’iPhone 18 Pro Max, contre une vingtaine de minutes auparavant. Avec un chargeur Anker de 140 W, j’ai atteint 40 % en 15 minutes et une charge complète en 1 h 09. C’est plus lent que ce qu’annonce Apple, et l’explication tient au chargeur.
Pour profiter des 15 minutes annoncées, la puissance du chargeur ne suffit pas : il doit aussi prendre en charge l’USB Power Delivery 3.1 et l’AVS. Mon bloc secteur n’a pas négocié ce profil. Avec la plupart des chargeurs existants, la recharge reste donc comparable à celle du 17 Pro Max.
Apple iPhone 18 Pro MaxRéseau et communication
Comme l’iPhone 18 Pro, le Pro Max conserve la puce Apple N1, avec Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 6 et Thread. La nouveauté majeure est son modem Apple C2, qui remplace celui de Qualcomm, sauf sur le Pro Max américain.
Apple annonce des envois de données plus rapides et une consommation réduite de 15 % par rapport à son précédent modem, le C1X. Côté consommation, mes mesures d’autonomie vont dans ce sens. En revanche, je n’ai pas l’impression d’avoir des débits supérieurs en 5G sur le réseau Bouygues que j’utilise dans les Yvelines.
En France, le téléphone accepte une nano-SIM et une eSIM, ou deux eSIM. Il conserve aussi l’Ultra Wideband, le NFC, le GPS double fréquence, les fonctions satellite et un port USB-C à 10 Gbit/s adapté aux usages vidéo professionnels.
Apple iPhone 18 Pro MaxPrix et disponibilité
L’iPhone 18 Pro Max est actuellement l’iPhone le plus cher. Il est décliné en plusieurs versions de 256 Go à 2 To et aucune n’a été épargnée par la montée des prix.
| Stockage | iPhone 17 Pro Max | iPhone 18 Pro Max | Différence | 
|---|---|---|---|
| 256 Go | 1 479 € | 1 629 € | +150 € | 
| 512 Go | 1 729 € | 1 879 € | +150 € | 
| 1 To | 1 979 € | 2 379 € | +400 € | 
| 2 To | 2 479 € | 3 129 € | +650 € | 
De 150 à 650 euros, voilà la douloureuse supplémentaire qu’il faut ajouter pour s’offrir un iPhone 18 Pro Max cette année. Toute l’industrie réhausse ses tarifs avec les nouvelles gammes, Apple est loin d’être un cas isolé.

articles.title: Vertrauliche Informationen verraten: OpenAI feuert drei Mitarbeiter
articles.text:
Vertrauliche Informationen verraten: OpenAI feuert drei Mitarbeiter
Nach der Aufregung um eigenständige Hacking-Aktivitäten von Künstlicher Intelligenz des ChatGPT-Entwicklers OpenAI hat die Firma drei an der Aufarbeitung beteiligte Experten entlassen. Sie hätten gegen interne Regeln zum Umgang mit vertraulichen Informationen verstoßen, teilte OpenAI zur Begründung mit. Zugleich betonte die KI-Firma, niemand sei gefeuert worden, weil er Sicherheitsbedenken geäußert habe. Das Fehlverhalten sei über das Teilen von Informationen mit einer externen Analysefirma hinausgegangen, hieß es ohne nähere Details.
Das Wall Street Journal hatte zuvor unter Berufung auf informierte Personen die Namen der drei entlassenen Mitarbeiter genannt. OpenAI sprach nur von zwei Sicherheitsforschern und einem Programm-Manager, wollte die Namen auf Anfrage aber nicht bestätigen. Auch die drei von der Zeitung genannten Personen äußerten sich zunächst nicht. OpenAI zufolge war das für die Beschäftigung nötige Vertrauen nicht mehr gegeben.
Negativ-Schlagzeilen für OpenAI
In dem bisher aufsehenerregendsten Fall war Künstliche Intelligenz des ChatGPT-Entwicklers aus einer abgesicherten Testumgebung ausgebrochen und hatte sich ungeplant in Computer der Plattform Hugging Face gehackt. Zur Aufarbeitung des Vorfalls hatte OpenAI für einige Tage auf KI-Sicherheit spezialisierte externe Experten herangeholt, die später tiefgreifende Einblicke in die Vorgehensweise der Software veröffentlichten. Zumindest einer der vom Wall Street Journal gefeuerten Mitarbeiter hatte erwähnt, Anlaufstelle für die externen Analysten gewesen zu sein.
[crosslink]
Ende September wurde auch bekannt, dass OpenAI nach einem neuen Zwischenfall das Training der leistungsstärksten Künstlichen Intelligenz ausgesetzt hat. Bei dem Vorfall schaffte es ein KI-Modell in einem Test, Antworten von einem externen Chatbot zu bekommen, obwohl es eigentlich keinen Internetzugang haben sollte. Die Software habe jedoch eine Lücke in den Netzwerkeinstellungen gefunden und ausgenutzt, hieß es. Das Eingeständnis war besonders heikel, da OpenAI die Sicherheitsvorkehrungen nach der Hacking-Attacke auf Hugging Face verschärft hatte. Zudem strich die Firma die Veröffentlichung eines neuen KI-Modells nach Sicherheitsbedenken.
Selbstregulierung in den USA
Forscher aus der Branche warnten zuletzt mehrfach vor einem existenziellen Risiko für die Menschheit, wenn leistungsstarke Künstliche Intelligenz außer Kontrolle geraten sollte. OpenAI-Chef Sam Altman solidarisierte sich mit dem Vorschlag des Konkurrenten Dario Amodei vom KI-Entwickler Anthropic, die Entwicklung der fähigsten KI-Modelle abzubremsen. Nach einem Treffen mit US-Präsident Donald Trump verpflichteten sich die Unternehmen jedoch nur, die Sicherheitsvorkehrungen zu stärken und externe Beobachter zuzulassen. Er wolle, dass sich die Unternehmen gegenseitig beaufsichtigten, sagte Trump.

articles.title: La batterie des AirPods 5 peut enfin être remplacée, mais il vous faut un sèche-cheveux
articles.text:
Le laboratoire de démontage iFixit a passé les AirPods 5 sur sa table d’opération et leur attribue un 2 sur 10, « la meilleure note que nous ayons attribuée à des AirPods ». Tous les modèles précédents plafonnaient à zéro depuis le tout premier verdict, fin 2016, qui rangeait déjà les écouteurs parmi les pires appareils jamais passés sur l’établi. L’écart tient à un progrès unique, l’extraction des batteries des écouteurs, et à la méthode retenue pour y parvenir.
Un sèche-cheveux, une pince, et la batterie sort
La procédure tient du salon de coiffure : un sèche-cheveux ramollit la colle de l’écouteur, un serre-joint le maintient en place le temps que la chaleur agisse. Une paire de pinces extrait ensuite la batterie. Le choix de l’outil relève d’une doctrine assumée, « les gens ont plus souvent un sèche-cheveux qu’un pistolet thermique ou une station à air chaud ». Techniciens aguerris et bricoleurs motivés peuvent espérer un taux de réussite correct, de l’aveu même des démonteurs.
Le progrès vient d’un connecteur à ergots repris du design des AirPods 3, un format que les AirPods 4 avaient délaissé et qui congédie les minuscules soudures des générations récentes. Une fois la colle vaincue, la batterie se débranche facilement. Les exemplaires gauche et droit affichent en revanche des polarités inversées et refusent d’être intervertis. Le boîtier de charge n’a rien appris : ses coutures serrées ont eu raison du démontage, et l’exemplaire sacrifié pour l’exercice n’y a pas survécu.
Bruxelles avait pourtant signé la dispense
La Commission européenne a adopté le 14 juillet 2026 une série d’exemptions à son règlement sur les batteries. Les AirPods et l’Apple Watch y échappent à l’obligation de batterie remplaçable par l’utilisateur. L’argument retenu tient au risque d’infiltration d’eau dans un boîtier scellé mal refermé, un raisonnement déjà appliqué aux brosses à dents électriques. La dispense s’ouvre aux produits où le retrait de la batterie crée un risque, ou quand « aucun accès utilisateur réaliste ne peut être aménagé avec les méthodes de fabrication actuelles » ; l’iPhone profitait déjà d’un statut comparable dans la version d’origine du texte. L’ensemble doit encore passer devant le Parlement et le Conseil.
Apple a donc amélioré un produit que le régulateur venait précisément de dispenser d’effort, et deux mois seulement séparent l’adoption de la dispense de l’arrivée des écouteurs remaniés. Les démonteurs, qui jugent l’ensemble « toujours décevant à bien des égards », rappellent de leur côté que « d’autres fabricants ont déjà résolu ce défi d’ingénierie » (coucou les Fairbuds).
Présentés le 9 septembre avec une réduction de bruit active désormais de série, les AirPods 5 se vendent dès 149 € en France (bien que des offres à 120 € aient déjà fait leur apparition). Ils restent des écouteurs pénibles à ouvrir, aux batteries jumelles incompatibles et au boîtier sacrificiel. La paire gagne pourtant l’essentiel : le droit de survivre à sa première batterie fatiguée, sans passer par la case rachat.

articles.title: Brazil’s future depends on science
articles.text:
Brazil’s future depends on science, a key area for strengthening policies and ensuring the country’s sovereignty in the face of new challenges. However, an analysis by the Brazilian Academy of Sciences (ABC), based on the organization’s assessments and proposals over the past four election cycles, shows that we still have a long way to go in this regard.
Although Brazil has increased the number of PhD holders (from 10,000 in 2005 to about 24,000 in 2023) and established legal frameworks to incentivize research, funding for science remains insufficient and marked by instability.
The proposal, advocated for decades, to allocate 2% of GDP to the sector has never been implemented, despite significant improvements in the budget in recent years.
Data from the Ministry of Science, Technology, and Innovation (MCTI) indicate that national spending on research and development reached 1.2% of GDP in 2023 — a percentage higher than the average for Latin America and the Caribbean, but still below the global average of 1.92% or the 2.7% recorded by member countries of the OECD.
Meanwhile, the country faces a series of challenges in which investment in research is the foundation of every policy — from the need to train professionals attuned to new demands, such as Artificial Intelligence (AI) and policies regarding critical minerals, to investment in technologies for the energy transition, for example.
This does not mean, however, that science should limit itself to these issues alone — quite the contrary. Investment in research must be guided by a focus on people, not merely by market demands. It is also necessary to safeguard support for basic research, which is fundamental to the advancement of knowledge.
Structural Bottlenecks
An ABC document released in July 2026 with proposals for the presidential candidates on the upcoming Oct. 5 election shows that structural bottlenecks persist in the country. Science already has solutions to address them based on available evidence.
One example comes from education. Despite universal access, the country faces stagnation in quality and persistent regional inequalities. Ensuring literacy at the appropriate age and providing an attractive, vocational high school education are essential to curbing dropout rates.
In the climate arena, the degradation of biomes and the intensification of extreme weather events show that climate change is no longer an issue to be addressed later. Warnings about the climate are not an exaggeration; they represent a commitment to the health, economy, and well-being of the population. In this sense, policies aimed at ending deforestation and phasing out fossil fuels are imperative.
Another example comes from the debate surrounding critical minerals. Although Brazil is rich in these resources, it still relies heavily on other countries for refining and processing. A strategy is needed that integrates sustainable exploitation, technological development, and industrialization, ensuring national sovereignty.
Stable Public Policies Are Lacking
Proposals to address Brazil’s problems are already on the table, but implementation, continuity, and governance are lacking. Stable public policies, continuous investment in education and research, valuing scientists, and strengthening scientific institutions are fundamental to addressing both persistent bottlenecks and new challenges.
On the eve of the elections, we must remember that science is not a separate field, isolated from others, toward which current candidates for various executive and legislative offices can choose whether or not to show an affinity.
Science must be the central pillar of all proposals for those elected in this Sunday’s election or who advance to a runoff. And voters need to be mindful of this.
Science must be a matter of State policy — a structural pillar, not a secondary agenda. Investing in research funding ensures the country’s ability to monitor risks, seek solutions to its own needs, train qualified professionals, and respond quickly to emergencies.
Emergencies ranging from health to climate, encompassing various other areas. It is also a way to transform knowledge into well-being, economic development, and political autonomy.
With elections for president, governors, and — most importantly —representatives and senators, Brazil has a new opportunity to choose science this Sunday.
For voters, it is a chance to reject those who disregard science or doubt its importance. For candidates, it is a chance to incorporate evidence-based proposals, avoid the unnecessary waste of resources, and demonstrate their commitment to actions focused on Brazil’s needs — not those of other countries.

articles.title: How American Political Campaigns Are Using AI—and What They're Spending on the Tools - Schneier on Security
articles.text:
How American Political Campaigns Are Using AI—and What They’re Spending on the Tools
This essay was written with Nathan E. Sanders, and originally appeared in The Guardian.
New campaign finance disclosure data shines a light on which US political campaigns are using AI tools and how much they are spending on them.
Candidates’, parties’ and committees’ spending reveals that AI is fast becoming an essential tool of politics. The candidates themselves are quiet about how they are using the technology in their own campaigns. It’s a sensitive issue that we have been tracking closely since we started writing our book, Rewiring Democracy, which examined how AI is beginning to influence politics. A September 2025 Pew survey of Americans found that more than 70% would think less of a candidate if they used AI to help write a speech.
Itemized expenditure disclosure data from the US Federal Election Commission, dating back to 2020, reveals at least $17m in disclosed spending on AI technology vendors across 523 federal candidates and campaigns. Data from four states, California, Colorado, Massachusetts and Washington, provides a more localized picture going back to 2022.
Beginning with the AI behemoths, at least 80 federal campaigns and committees have reported spending with OpenAI since 2024. The total spending is not huge: only about $50,000 reported, skewing slightly more Republican than Democratic. The Republican National Committee is the largest overall buyer, with nearly $10,000 in reported expenses. Top individual users include the campaigns of Republicans Mike Lawler, John Kennedy and Bill Cassidy, as well as the California Democrats Ro Khanna and Ted Lieu. Most of these expenses are listed as office expenses, subscriptions to ChatGPT for staff, or research tools, rather than as specific political services. The company’s policies prohibit some political uses of their ChatGPT tool.
OpenAI’s biggest competitor, Anthropic, has rapidly built a similar level of usage, but with a different split. At least 65 candidates or committees now report paying the Claude maker in 2026, up from essentially zero in previous years, with a nearly two-to-one Democrat-to-Republican ratio. However, the largest individual user is the campaign of Tom Cotton, a Republican senator from Arkansas, who reported more than $4,000 in spend on Anthropic software in his June filing. Other major users are the Montana independent Senate candidate Seth Bodnar and Jason Knapp, who lost a Democratic House primary in Virginia, and the Democratic Alaska Senate candidate Mary Peltola.
Candidates use either Claude or ChatGPT, rarely both, according to the disclosures. Only about 12% of campaigns or committees using either tool reported expenditures to both vendors. The Democratic lean of Anthropic usage may reflect the company’s alleged liberal skew and clashes with the Trump administration.
In contrast, Elon Musk’s xAI caters to Republican interests and, accordingly, its meager usage comes almost entirely from the political right. Just seven federal and two state-level candidates or committees have reported paying xAI, a total of about $5,000, the majority of which was spent by the presidential campaign of RFK Jr in 2024, but also includes Republicans Dave McCormick and Thomas Massie.
More dollars go to the vendors specializing in political campaign applications of AI. For years, AmplifAI, which provides automated text messaging, essentially a new iteration on robocalling technology, was a dominant target of spending, soaking up $4.7m in campaign spending in the 2022 cycle alone. It was used heavily by Democratic candidates including Mark Kelly, Joe Biden, Bernie Sanders and Adam Schiff. Spending on AmplifAI, now owned by the troubled media conglomerate Triller, seems to have tapered off in the years since 2022.
The new rising Democratic solution for AI-powered text messaging is Daisychain, which has so far garnered about $300,000 in reported candidate spend in the 2026 cycle—up from only about $50,000 reported in 2024. More than half of this year’s spending comes from the Senate campaign of Democrat Abdul El-Sayed in Michigan.
The closest equivalent on the Republican side has been Campaign Nucleus, associated with former Trump campaign manager Brad Parscale. The AI-powered voter engagement tool has attracted six-figure spending from the Republican National Committee, multiple PACs aligned with Donald Trump, and five-figure investments from Mike Johnson, Kari Lake and other candidates. It is displacing the legacy Republican-serving texting vendor Prompt.io, which has retained about $375,000 in 2026 spending to date, down from more than $500,000 in the 2022 cycle. But it continues to be used: the A More Affordable California PAC sponsored by Uber has single-handedly spent more than $1m on Prompt.io in 2026. The Republican Massachusetts gubernatorial nominee Michael Minogue has been a recurring customer, as has the failed Republican California gubernatorial candidate Ché Ahn and Republican-aligned Super PAC Neighbors for a Better Colorado.
At the state level
At the state level, the AI spending is smaller but growing fast. Across the four states studied, we found a total of at least $92,000 in spending confidently attributable to modern generative AI vendors since 2022. The spending is spread across at least 108 candidates and committees. The growth has been explosive; there has already been about 10 times the amount of state-level AI spending reported in 2026 as there was in all of 2024.
Much of the state spending mirrors federal patterns. Daisychain again has the highest overall spend, and OpenAI and Claude dominate among the general-purpose AI vendors. DonorAtlas—the AI-powered prospect research tool—sticks out for its usage in these states, sitting behind only Daisychain and OpenAI and buoyed up by nearly $4,000 in spending by the California Democratic party.
Even though it has dominated so much media conversation, few candidates seem to be reporting spending on AI tools designed specifically to create synthetic audio and video, also known as “deepfakes”. We found just six federal candidates or committees reporting spending on the popular AI audio generator tool from ElevenLabs, with total spending of about $1,400 led by independent candidate for Colorado’s sixth congressional district Samir Witta. The AI image generator service Midjourney has five reported federal campaign or committee users reporting about $1,600, led by Sholdon Daniels, the Republican primary runner-up in the Texas 30th district. Combined, those two firms had less than $100 in reported spend across the four states.
However, recent data from the Wesleyan Media Project shows that at least 164 political ads in this cycle have included AI-generated media, supported by at least $80m in ad spending. What this illustrates is that candidate and committee disclosure reports are just the tip of the iceberg. They don’t cover spending on AI by political consultants, media firms and other vendors hired by the campaigns or by PACs, or independent committees raising and spending money aimed at boosting candidates’ campaigns. Those entities aren’t required to disclose detailed expenditure reports, and are very likely where the bulk of campaign AI usage is happening.
Since a large fraction of all spending in the campaign cycle will happen in the final weeks leading to November, much remains to be seen about the totality of how campaigns will leverage AI and what impact its use will have on voters’ decisions.

articles.title: Avant l'attaque du Venezuela, Trump a demandé son avis à Grok, le chatbot d'Elon Musk — Frandroid
articles.text:
Le magazine Time a publié ce jeudi 1er octobre « What Trump Has Built », un long portrait de Donald Trump signé par le journaliste Eric Cortellessa. On y apprend qu’en décembre 2025, Elon Musk est revenu dans le Bureau ovale pour une réunion restée secrète.
C’était environ sept mois après son départ du DOGE, la commission chargée de couper dans les dépenses fédérales. Donald Trump a passé « des heures » à poser des questions à Grok, le chatbot de xAI, la société d’intelligence artificielle de Musk. L’une d’elles portait sur le Venezuela, un mois avant que l’armée américaine n’aille y capturer le président Nicolás Maduro.
Le président américain voulait savoir comment les Vénézuéliens réagiraient si les États-Unis capturaient Maduro. Un responsable présent à la réunion raconte que Grok a répondu que Maduro était un dictateur répressif et profondément impopulaire. Toujours d’après lui, le chatbot a ajouté que beaucoup de Vénézuéliens fêteraient sans doute sa chute.
À ce moment-là, Washington et Caracas étaient déjà en conflit ouvert. Depuis septembre 2025, Donald Trump ordonnait des frappes militaires contre des bateaux vénézuéliens qu’il accusait de transporter de la drogue vers les États-Unis.
Des fêtes dans la rue, et un Grok « ingénieux »
Les États-Unis ont envahi le Venezuela le 3 janvier 2026 et capturé Maduro. Ensuite, des Vénézuéliens sont descendus dans la rue pour fêter son départ. D’après des responsables cités par Time, Donald Trump en a conclu que Grok était « ingénieux ».
On ignore quel poids la réponse du chatbot a pesé face aux avis des militaires et des diplomates. Time ajoute que Donald Trump s’émerveille des capacités de l’IA depuis son retour au pouvoir, et qu’il écoute de plus en plus les patrons de la tech qui lui font la cour.
Grok sert déjà l’armée américaine
TechCrunch, qui a relayé l’article de Time, rappelle que Grok est depuis entré au Pentagone. En juin 2026, Cameron Stanley, responsable du numérique et de l’IA au ministère de la Défense, a déclaré sous serment que Grok Gov, la version du chatbot réservée au gouvernement, avait servi pendant la guerre contre l’Iran.
xAI avait signé le 23 février 2026 un accord qui autorise l’armée à utiliser Grok dans ses systèmes classifiés, cinq jours avant le début de l’offensive en Iran.
Grok n’est pas le seul modèle d’IA au service du Pentagone. OpenAI a aussi signé un accord avec le ministère, alors qu’Anthropic est en conflit avec l’administration sur l’usage militaire de ses modèles.
Elon Musk retrouve aussi un rôle officiel dans l’administration, a priori le premier depuis son départ du DOGE. Ce mercredi 30 septembre, le secrétaire à la Défense Pete Hegseth a lancé Project Meridian, une étude sur les armes et les champs de bataille de demain. Elon Musk la codirige avec Palmer Luckey, fondateur du fabricant de drones militaires Anduril, et Newt Gingrich, ancien président de la Chambre des représentants. Ils ont 120 jours pour rendre leurs conclusions, donc jusqu’à fin janvier 2027.

articles.title: Engineering Multipole Resonances in Dielectric Metasurfaces for Transmission, Reflection, and Absorption Control
articles.text: Dielectric metasurfaces have moved to the forefront of nanophotonics, offering flat, low-loss alternatives to conventional bulk optical elements for controlling the amplitude, phase, and polarization of light. These structures are of growing interest to researchers and engineers working on sensing, energy harvesting, and flat optics, as their performance hinges on precisely engineered optical resonances. Full-wave finite element simulation, combined with semianalytical multipole decomposition in the COMSOL Multiphysics® software, gives us a way to not only predict these resonances but also uncover their underlying physical origins. In this webinar, Dr. Pavel Terekhov, postdoctoral researcher at National Institute of Standards and Technology, will trace how a single quadrumer meta-atom, originally studied for its magnetic octupole response, evolves into two distinct light manipulation regimes. He will first revisit the foundational single-particle results that motivated this work, then show how arranging quadrumers into a periodic crystalline silicon metasurface produces anomalous absorption enhancement, governed by two independent multipole mechanisms coexisting in the same structure. Building on this, he will then introduce ongoing work on a gallium nitride metasurface, where the complex interplay of four different multipoles is used to sculpt reflection and transmission spectra including the quasi-bound-states-in-the-continuum (q-BIC) manipulation. Attendees will see how COMSOL Multiphysics® and multipole decomposition connect full-wave simulation and analytical insight, turning abstract resonance behavior into physically interpretable design rules. The broader takeaway is that multipole-based simulation is not just a diagnostic tool but a design strategy: It enables the on-demand tailoring of absorption, reflection, and transmission in dielectric metasurfaces, with direct relevance to sensing, energy harvesting, and future optical device applications. Key Takeaways: Learn about modeling multipole resonances in dielectric metasurfaces using full-wave finite element simulation and semianalytical multipole decomposition in COMSOL Multiphysics®. See how multipole-based simulation can be used to understand and control absorption, reflection, and transmission in silicon and gallium nitride metasurfaces. Explore how different multipole mechanisms, including quasi-bound states in the continuum (q-BICs), can be engineered to tailor optical responses for sensing, energy harvesting, and flat optics. Gain insights into how simulation and multipole decomposition can help researchers and engineers turn complex resonance behavior into practical design strategies for future optical devices. articles.title: Sony anuncia QSSR, nova tecnologia que melhora gráficos do PS5
articles.text:
A Sony anunciou o Quick Spectral Super Resolution (QSSR), uma nova tecnologia de upscaling que promete melhorar a qualidade de imagem dos jogos no PlayStation 5. Diferentemente do PSSR, recurso disponível no PS5 Pro, a novidade funcionará também no modelo padrão do console.
Segundo a empresa, o QSSR é uma evolução de suas tecnologias de reconstrução de imagem e será disponibilizado amplamente para desenvolvedores do ecossistema PlayStation.
Os primeiros jogos a receber o recurso são Marvel’s Wolverine e Ghost of Yōtei, que ganham atualizações com o QSSR como uma opção gráfica adicional.
O que muda com o QSSR no PS5?
Tecnologias de upscaling permitem que um jogo seja renderizado internamente em uma resolução menor e tenha sua imagem reconstruída para uma resolução superior. Na prática, isso pode ajudar os desenvolvedores a equilibrar qualidade visual e desempenho.
No caso do QSSR, a promessa é melhorar especialmente a estabilidade da imagem e a reprodução de pequenos detalhes.
Uma análise do Digital Foundry classificou o potencial da tecnologia como “notável”. Em Marvel’s Wolverine, o veículo identificou maior estabilidade temporal, aumento do nível de detalhes e redução de artefatos visuais, principalmente em elementos em movimento.
Já em Ghost of Yōtei, a diferença seria menos evidente, em parte porque o título já apresentava boa qualidade de imagem antes da implementação da tecnologia.
QSSR não substitui o PSSR do PS5 Pro
Apesar das semelhanças, o novo recurso não deve ser confundido com o PlayStation Spectral Super Resolution (PSSR) presente no PS5 Pro.
A própria Sony continua tratando o PSSR como sua principal solução de reconstrução de imagem. O diferencial do QSSR está justamente em levar parte dos avanços obtidos nessa área para os consoles PS5 padrão.
Mike Fitzgerald, chefe de tecnologia da Insomniac Games, afirma que o QSSR acrescenta maior clareza e estabilidade aos ambientes de Marvel’s Wolverine, permitindo destacar detalhes de cenários movimentados.
Jasmin Patry, engenheira-chefe de renderização da Sucker Punch, também destacou a capacidade da tecnologia de reproduzir pequenos detalhes dos personagens e ambientes com maior estabilidade.
Com a Sony planejando oferecer a ferramenta para mais desenvolvedores, Marvel’s Wolverine e Ghost of Yōtei devem ser apenas os primeiros títulos a utilizar QSSR no PS5.
